sentences.zh: 宗室十五王 太祖諸子一

translations.literal: Fifteen Princes of the Imperial Clan: Sons of the Founding Emperor, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen Princes of the Imperial Clan: Sons of the Founding Emperor, Part One

sentences.zh: 明制，皇子封親王，授金冊金寶，歲祿萬石，府置官屬。

translations.literal: Under Ming institutions, imperial sons were enfeoffed as princes of the first rank, granted golden patent books and golden seals, received an annual stipend of ten thousand piculs, and had official staffs appointed in their princedoms.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming law, an emperor's sons were enfeoffed as princes of the first rank, given golden patent books and golden seals, granted ten thousand piculs in annual stipend, and provided with a full staff in their princedoms.

sentences.zh: 護衛甲士少者三千人，多者至萬九千人，隸籍兵部。

translations.literal: Their guard armored soldiers numbered no fewer than three thousand and as many as nineteen thousand, registered under the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Their princely guards ranged from three thousand armored troops to as many as nineteen thousand, all registered with the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 冕服車旗邸第，下天子一等。

translations.literal: Their ceremonial caps and robes, chariots, banners, and mansions were one grade below the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Their regalia, chariots, banners, and residences stood one rank below the emperor's.

sentences.zh: 公侯大臣伏而拜謁，無敢鈞禮。

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, and great ministers prostrated themselves in obeisance when paying calls; none dared treat them as equals in ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, marquises, and senior ministers bowed low when they came to call; none presumed to meet them as equals in ritual.

sentences.zh: 親王嫡長子，年及十歲，則授金冊金寶，立為王世子，長孫立為世孫，冠服視一品。

translations.literal: When a prince's eldest son by the principal consort reached ten years of age, he was granted a golden patent book and golden seal and installed as heir to the princedom; the eldest grandson was installed as heir to the heir, and their caps and robes were treated as first rank.
translations.idiomatic: When a prince's eldest son by the principal wife turned ten, he received a golden patent and seal and was named heir to the princedom; the eldest grandson was named heir to the heir, and both wore regalia equivalent to the first rank.

sentences.zh: 諸子年十歲，則授塗金銀冊銀寶，封為郡王。

translations.literal: When other sons reached ten years of age, they were granted gilded silver patent books and silver seals and enfeoffed as princes of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Other sons, at age ten, received gilded silver patents and silver seals and were enfeoffed as princes of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 嫡長子為郡王世子，嫡長孫則授長孫，冠服視二品。

translations.literal: The eldest son by the principal consort became heir to the commandery princedom; the eldest grandson by the principal line was granted the title of eldest grandson, and their caps and robes were treated as second rank.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son by the principal wife became heir to the second-rank princedom; the eldest grandson of the principal line received the title of eldest grandson, and both wore regalia equivalent to the second rank.

sentences.zh: 諸子授鎮國將軍，孫輔國將軍，曾孫奉國將軍，四世孫鎮國中尉，五世孫輔國中尉，六世以下皆奉國中尉。

translations.literal: Other sons received the title Defender-General of the State; grandsons received Supporter-General of the State; great-grandsons received Sustainer-General of the State; fourth-generation descendants received Defender-Commandant of the State; fifth-generation descendants received Supporter-Commandant of the State; from the sixth generation downward all received Sustainer-Commandant of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Sons received the rank of Defender-General of the State; grandsons, Supporter-General; great-grandsons, Sustainer-General; in the fourth generation, Defender-Commandant; in the fifth, Supporter-Commandant; and from the sixth generation on, all held the rank of Sustainer-Commandant of the State.

sentences.zh: 其生也請名，其長也請婚，祿之終身，喪葬予費，親親之誼篤矣。

translations.literal: At birth they petitioned for a name; when grown they petitioned for marriage; they received stipends for life and funeral expenses were granted—the affection due to kin was profound indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Names were requested at birth and marriages at maturity; stipends lasted a lifetime and burial costs were provided—the dynasty's care for its own blood was deep indeed.

sentences.zh: 考二百餘年之間，宗姓實繁，賢愚雜出。

translations.literal: Considering more than two hundred years, the imperial surname had truly multiplied, and the worthy and the foolish emerged in mixture.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than two centuries the imperial clan had grown vast indeed, and the capable and the worthless appeared side by side.

sentences.zh: 今據所紀載，自太祖時追封祔廟十五王以及列朝所封者，著於篇。

translations.literal: Now, according to what is recorded, from the fifteen princes posthumously enfeoffed and enshrined in the ancestral temple in the Founding Emperor's time down through those enfeoffed in successive reigns, they are set forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: What follows records, from the fifteen princes posthumously enfeoffed and enshrined under the Founding Emperor through those enfeoffed in later reigns, all that the annals preserve.

sentences.zh: 而郡王以下有行義事實可采者，世系亦得附見焉。

translations.literal: As for those below the rank of second-rank prince whose conduct and deeds were worth recording, their lines may also be appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Where princes of lower rank left conduct or deeds worth noting, their lines are included as well.

sentences.zh: 宗室十五王

translations.literal: Fifteen Princes of the Imperial Clan
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen Princes of the Imperial Clan

translations.idiomatic: Sons of the Founding Emperor, Part One

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Zhu Shuang; Prince of Qianyang Zhu Chenglie; Prince of Jin Zhu □; Prince of Qingcheng Zhu Jixuan; Prince of Xihe Zhu Qisu and Xin Die; Prince of Zhou Zhu Su; Prince of Zhenping Zhu Youhuang; Prince of Boping Zhu An Shui Xu; Prince of Nanling Zhu Mu□ying; Defender-Commandant of the State Zhu Mu□qie and Defender-General of the State Zhu An Shui Kan; Defender-Commandant of the State Zhu Qinyun; Prince of Chu Zhu Zhen; Prince of Wugang Zhu Xianhuai; Prince of Qi Zhu Fu; Prince of Tan Zhu Zi; Prince of Zhao Zhu □ji; Prince of Lu Zhu Tan; Prince of Guishan Zhu Danghong; Supporter-General of the State Zhu Dangfen; Sustainer-General of the State Zhu Jiangen; Prince of Anqiu Zhu Dangsui; Shou Jinlin.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter treats the Prince of Qin, Zhu Shuang; the Prince of Qianyang, Zhu Chenglie; the Prince of Jin, Zhu □; the Prince of Qingcheng, Zhu Jixuan; the Princes of Xihe, Zhu Qisu and Xin Die; the Prince of Zhou, Zhu Su; the Prince of Zhenping, Zhu Youhuang; the Prince of Boping, Zhu An Shui Xu; the Prince of Nanling, Zhu Mu□ying; the Defender-Commandants Zhu Mu□qie and Zhu Qinyun and the Defender-General Zhu An Shui Kan; the Prince of Chu, Zhu Zhen; the Prince of Wugang, Zhu Xianhuai; the Princes of Qi and Tan, Zhu Fu and Zhu Zi; the Prince of Zhao, Zhu □ji; the Prince of Lu, Zhu Tan; the Prince of Guishan, Zhu Danghong; the Supporter-General Zhu Dangfen; the Sustainer-General Zhu Jiangen; the Prince of Anqiu, Zhu Dangsui; and Shou Jinlin.

sentences.zh: 熙祖，二子。

translations.literal: Emperor Xi had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xi had two sons.

sentences.zh: 長仁祖，次壽春王，俱王太后生。

translations.literal: The eldest was Emperor Ren; the second was Prince of Shouchun—both born of Empress Dowager Wang.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest was Emperor Ren; the second was the Prince of Shouchun—both sons of Empress Dowager Wang.

sentences.zh: 壽春王四子，長霍丘王，次下蔡王，次安豐王，次蒙城王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shouchun had four sons: the eldest was Prince of Huoqiu; next Prince of Xiaocai; next Prince of Anfeng; and next Prince of Mengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shouchun had four sons: the eldest became Prince of Huoqiu, followed by the Princes of Xiaocai, Anfeng, and Mengcheng.

sentences.zh: 霍丘王一子，寶應王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Huoqiu had one son, Prince of Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Huoqiu had one son, the Prince of Baoying.

sentences.zh: 安豐王四子，六安王、來安王、都梁王、英山王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Anfeng had four sons: Princes of Lu'an, Lai'an, Duliang, and Yingshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Anfeng had four sons: the Princes of Lu'an, Lai'an, Duliang, and Yingshan.

sentences.zh: 下蔡、蒙城及寶應、六安諸王先卒，皆無後。

translations.literal: The princes of Xiaocai, Mengcheng, Baoying, and Lu'an all died first and left no heirs.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Xiaocai, Mengcheng, Baoying, and Lu'an all predeceased him and left no descendants.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年追封，二年定從祀禮，祔享祖廟東西廡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu they were posthumously enfeoffed; in the second year the rites of collateral sacrifice were fixed, and they were enshrined for shared worship in the eastern and western side halls of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 they received posthumous enfeoffments; in Hongwu 2 the rites of collateral sacrifice were established, and they were installed for worship in the east and west wings of the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 壽春、霍丘、安豐、蒙城四王，皆以王妃配食。

translations.literal: The four princes of Shouchun, Huoqiu, Anfeng, and Mengcheng all had their consorts join them in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: For the four princes of Shouchun, Huoqiu, Anfeng, and Mengcheng, their consorts shared the sacrificial offerings.

sentences.zh: 蒙城王妃田氏早寡，有節行，太祖甚重之。

translations.literal: The consort of the Prince of Mengcheng, Lady Tian, was widowed early and observed chaste conduct; the Founding Emperor held her in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tian, consort of the Prince of Mengcheng, was widowed young and lived with exemplary fidelity; the Founding Emperor esteemed her deeply.

sentences.zh: 十王、四妃墓在鳳陽白塔祠，官歲祀焉。

translations.literal: The tombs of the ten princes and four consorts were at the White Pagoda Shrine in Fengyang, where officials made annual sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The ten princes and four consorts were buried at the White Pagoda Shrine in Fengyang, where the state performed annual sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 仁祖，四子。

translations.literal: Emperor Ren had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ren had four sons.

sentences.zh: 長南昌王，次盱眙王，次臨淮王，次太祖，俱陳太后生。

translations.literal: The eldest was Prince of Nanchang; next Prince of Xuyi; next Prince of Linhuai; and last the Founding Emperor—all born of Empress Dowager Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest was the Prince of Nanchang, followed by the Princes of Xuyi and Linhuai, and last the Founding Emperor—all sons of Empress Dowager Chen.

sentences.zh: 南昌王二子，長山陽王，無後，次文正。

translations.literal: The Prince of Nanchang had two sons: the eldest was Prince of Shanyang, who left no heir; the second was Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Nanchang had two sons: the elder, Prince of Shanyang, died without issue; the younger was Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 盱眙王一子，昭信王，無後。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xuyi had one son, Prince of Zhaoxin, who left no heir.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xuyi had one son, the Prince of Zhaoxin, who died without descendants.

sentences.zh: 臨淮王無子。

translations.literal: The Prince of Linhuai had no son.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Linhuai had no sons.

sentences.zh: 太祖起兵時，諸王皆前卒，獨文正在。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor raised his army, all the princes had already died; only Wenzheng was still alive.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor took up arms, all his brothers were already dead save Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，諸王皆追封從祀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu all the princes were posthumously enfeoffed and granted collateral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu reign all were posthumously enfeoffed and admitted to collateral worship.

sentences.zh: 文正以罪謫死。

translations.literal: Wenzheng was demoted for a crime and died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzheng was punished for a crime and died in banishment.

sentences.zh: 子守謙，封靖江王，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Shouqian was enfeoffed as Prince of Jingjiang and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouqian was enfeoffed as Prince of Jingjiang; his life is recorded in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 正德十一年，御史徐文華言：「宋儒程頤曰：『成人而無後者，祭終兄弟之孫之身。』

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhengde, Censor Xu Wenhua said: "The Song scholar Cheng Yi said: 'When an adult dies without heirs, sacrifice ends with the body of a brother's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 11, Censor Xu Wenhua argued: "The Song scholar Cheng Yi wrote: 'When a man dies without heirs, sacrifice ends with a brother's grandson.

sentences.zh: 蓋從祖而祔，亦從祖而毀，未有祖祧而祔食之孫獨存者。

translations.literal: Thus when one is enshrined with a collateral ancestor, one is removed with that collateral ancestor; there has never been a case where the main ancestral line was removed while a collateral grandson enshrined with it alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: One who is enshrined with a collateral forebear is removed when that forebear is removed; the main line of ancestors cannot be retired while a collateral grandson installed with them alone remains.

sentences.zh: 今懿、僖二祖既祧，太廟祔享諸王亦宜罷祀。」

translations.literal: Now that the Founding Emperor's father and grandfather have been removed from the main temple, the princes enshrined for shared worship in the Grand Temple should also cease to receive sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Now that Emperors Yi and Xi have been removed from the main temple, the princes enshrined there for collateral worship should cease to receive offerings as well.'

sentences.zh: 廷議不可，文華竟以妄言下獄。

translations.literal: The court deliberated and would not agree; Wenhua was ultimately imprisoned for reckless speech.
translations.idiomatic: The court rejected the proposal, and Wenhua was jailed in the end for reckless words.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中建九廟，東西廡如故。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign nine temples were built, and the eastern and western side halls remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing nine temples were erected, and the east and west wings were left as they had been.

sentences.zh: 九廟災，復同堂異室之制，祔十五王於兩序。

translations.literal: When the nine temples burned, the system of one hall with separate chambers was restored, and the fifteen princes were enshrined for collateral worship in the two wings.
translations.idiomatic: After fire destroyed the nine temples, the single-hall, separate-chamber arrangement was restored, and the fifteen princes were again installed for collateral worship in the two wings.

sentences.zh: 盱眙、臨淮王二妃配食。

translations.literal: The two consorts of the Princes of Xuyi and Linhuai joined in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The consorts of the Princes of Xuyi and Linhuai shared the sacrificial offerings.

sentences.zh: 南昌王妃王氏，後薨，祔葬皇陵，不配食。

translations.literal: The consort of the Prince of Nanchang, Lady Wang, died later and was buried by association at the imperial mausoleum, but did not join in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang, consort of the Prince of Nanchang, died later and was buried beside the imperial tombs, but did not share in the offerings.

sentences.zh: 太祖，二十六子。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor had twenty-six sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor had twenty-six sons.

sentences.zh: 高皇后生太子標、秦王樉、晉王□、成祖、周王橚。

translations.literal: Empress Gao bore the crown prince Biao, Prince of Qin Shuang, Prince of Jin □, the Yongle Emperor, and Prince of Zhou Su.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gao bore the crown prince Biao, the Princes of Qin and Jin (Zhu Shuang and Zhu □), the Yongle Emperor, and the Prince of Zhou, Zhu Su.

sentences.zh: 胡充妃生楚王楨。

translations.literal: Consort Hu Chong bore Prince of Chu Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Hu Chong bore Zhu Zhen, Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 達定妃生齊王榑、潭王梓。

translations.literal: Consort Da Ding bore Prince of Qi Fu and Prince of Tan Zi.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Da Ding bore the Princes of Qi and Tan, Zhu Fu and Zhu Zi.

sentences.zh: 郭寧妃生魯王檀。

translations.literal: Consort Guo Ning bore Prince of Lu Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Guo Ning bore Zhu Tan, Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 郭惠妃生蜀王椿、代王桂、谷王橞。

translations.literal: Consort Guo Hui bore Prince of Shu Chun, Prince of Dai Gui, and Prince of Gu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Guo Hui bore the Princes of Shu, Dai, and Gu—Zhu Chun, Zhu Gui, and Zhu Yan.

sentences.zh: 胡順妃生湘王柏。

translations.literal: Consort Hu Shun bore Prince of Xiang Bai.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Hu Shun bore Zhu Bai, Prince of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 韓妃生遼王植。

translations.literal: Consort Han bore Prince of Liao Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Han bore Zhu Zhi, Prince of Liao.

sentences.zh: 余妃生慶王□旃。

translations.literal: Consort Yu bore Prince of Qing □zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yu bore the Prince of Qing, Zhu □zhan.

sentences.zh: 楊妃生寧王權。

translations.literal: Consort Yang bore Prince of Ning Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang bore Zhu Quan, Prince of Ning.

sentences.zh: 周妃生岷王楩、韓王松。

translations.literal: Consort Zhou bore Prince of Min Bian and Prince of Han Song.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhou bore the Princes of Min and Han, Zhu Bian and Zhu Song.

sentences.zh: 趙貴妃生沈王模。

translations.literal: Noble Consort Zhao bore Prince of Shen Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Consort Zhao bore Zhu Mo, Prince of Shen.

sentences.zh: 李賢妃生唐王檉。

translations.literal: Consort Li Xian bore Prince of Tang Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Li Xian bore Zhu Cheng, Prince of Tang.

sentences.zh: 劉惠妃生郢王楝。

translations.literal: Consort Liu Hui bore Prince of Ying Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Liu Hui bore Zhu Dong, Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 葛麗妃生伊王□彝。

translations.literal: Consort Ge Li bore Prince of Yi □yi.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Ge Li bore the Prince of Yi, Zhu □yi.

sentences.zh: 而肅王柍母郜無名號。

translations.literal: The mother of Prince of Su Zhi, Lady Gao, had no formal title.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Su's mother, Lady Gao, held no formal consort rank.

sentences.zh: 趙王□巳、安王楹、皇子楠皆未詳所生母。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao □ji, Prince of An Ying, and the imperial son Nan—their birth mothers are not recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: For the Prince of Zhao Zhu □ji, the Prince of An Zhu Ying, and the imperial son Nan, the identity of their mothers is unknown.

sentences.zh: 秦愍王樉，太祖第二子。

translations.literal: Prince Min of Qin, Zhu Shuang, was the Founding Emperor's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Min of Qin, Zhu Shuang, was the Founding Emperor's second son.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the third year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He received his enfeoffment in Hongwu 3.

sentences.zh: 十一年就籓西安。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he took up his fief at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 11 he went to his fief at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 其年五月賜璽書曰：「關內之民，自元氏失政，不勝其敝。

translations.literal: That year in the fifth month an imperial letter was granted, saying: "The people within the passes, since the Yuan lost good government, have been unable to bear their afflictions.
translations.idiomatic: That May the emperor sent him a sealed letter: "The people of the Guanzhong region, since the Yuan lost the way of rule, have borne hardships beyond endurance.

sentences.zh: 今吾定天下，又有轉輸之勞，民未休息。

translations.literal: Now that I have settled the realm, there is again the labor of transport, and the people have not yet rested.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have pacified the realm, they still labor under transport levies and have scarcely had rest.

sentences.zh: 爾之國，若宮室已完，其不急之務悉已之。」

translations.literal: In your state, if the palaces are already finished, cease entirely all matters that are not urgent.
translations.idiomatic: In your domain, once your palaces are finished, put aside every task that is not urgent.

sentences.zh: 十五年八月，高皇后崩，與晉、燕諸王奔喪京師，十月還國。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifteenth year Empress Gao died; together with the princes of Jin and Yan he rushed to the capital for mourning and returned to his state in the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Hongwu 15, after Empress Gao's death, he hurried to the capital with the Princes of Jin and Yan and returned to his fief in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 十七年，皇后大祥，復來朝，尋遣還。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, at the great completion of mourning for the empress, he came to court again and was soon sent back.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 17, when the empress's mourning was completed, he came to court again and was soon sent home.

sentences.zh: 二十二年改大宗正院為宗人府，以樉為宗人令。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the Court of the Imperial Clan was renamed the Imperial Clan Court, and Shuang was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 22 the Court of the Imperial Clan became the Imperial Clan Court, and Shuang was named its director.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以樉多過失，召還京師，令皇太子巡視關陝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, because Shuang had many faults, he was summoned back to the capital and the crown prince was ordered to inspect Guanzhong and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 24, because Shuang had committed many faults, he was recalled to the capital and the crown prince was sent to inspect Guanzhong and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 太子還，為之解。

translations.literal: When the crown prince returned, he interceded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince returned, he spoke in Shuang's defense.

sentences.zh: 明年命歸籓。

translations.literal: The next year he was ordered to return to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was ordered back to his fief.

sentences.zh: 從弟臨潼王誠澯子昭王秉□嗣。

translations.literal: His younger cousin's son, Prince Zhao Zhu Bing□, succeeded from Prince of Lintong Zhu Chengzhan.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed to Zhu Bing□ of Zhao, son of Zhu Chengzhan, Prince of Lintong, a younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 十四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 子定王惟焯嗣，有賢行，有司以聞。

translations.literal: His son Prince Ding Zhu Weizhuo succeeded; he had worthy conduct, and the authorities reported it.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Weizhuo, Prince Ding, succeeded him; officials reported his exemplary conduct.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十九年，敕表以綽楔。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiajing an edict erected a commemorative tablet with a carved frame.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 19 the throne ordered a commemorative plaque with carved frame erected in his honor.

sentences.zh: 獻金助太廟工，益歲祿二百石，賜玉帶襲衣。

translations.literal: He presented gold to assist work on the Grand Temple; his annual stipend was increased by two hundred piculs, and he was granted a jade belt and court robes.
translations.idiomatic: He donated gold toward the Grand Temple project; his annual stipend rose by two hundred piculs, and he received a jade belt and ceremonial robes.

sentences.zh: 惟焯嘗奏請潼關以西、鳳翔以東河堧地，曰：「皇祖所賜先臣樉也。」

translations.literal: Weizhuo once memorialized requesting the river-bank lands west of Tong Pass and east of Fengxiang, saying: "These were granted by the imperial grandfather to my late forebear Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhuo once petitioned for the river-bank lands west of Tong Pass and east of Fengxiang, claiming they had been granted by the founding emperor to his ancestor Shuang.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書梁材執奏：「陝西外供三鎮，內給四王，民困已極。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Liang Cai memorialized firmly: "Shaanxi supplies the three garrisons abroad and four princes within; the people's distress has already reached its limit.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Liang Cai objected: "Shaanxi already feeds three frontier garrisons and four princely households; the people are at the breaking point.

sentences.zh: 豈得復奪堧地，濫給宗籓。」

translations.literal: How can we again seize river-bank lands and lavish them on the imperial clan?
translations.idiomatic: How can we strip away more river lands to lavish on the imperial clan?

sentences.zh: 詔如材言。

translations.literal: An edict followed Liang Cai's words.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ruled as Liang Cai urged.

sentences.zh: 二十三年薨，無子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died without a son.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-third year of the reign, leaving no heir.

sentences.zh: 再從子宣王懷埢由中尉嗣。

translations.literal: A second cousin once removed, Prince Xuan Zhu Huaiqiao, succeeded from the rank of commandant.
translations.idiomatic: A more distant cousin, Zhu Huaiqiao, Prince Xuan, succeeded from the rank of commandant.

sentences.zh: 奏以本祿千石贍諸宗，賜敕獎諭。

translations.literal: He memorialized that he used his own stipend of one thousand piculs to support the clan; an edict of commendation was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He reported using his thousand-picul stipend to support needy kinsmen and received an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 四十五年薨。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-fifth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 子靖王敬鎔嗣，萬歷四年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Jing Zhu Jingrong succeeded and died in the fourth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Jingrong, Prince Jing, succeeded him and died in Wanli 4.

sentences.zh: 子敬王誼旐嗣，十四年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Jing Zhu Yizhao succeeded and died in the fourteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Yizhao, Prince Jing, succeeded and died in the fourteenth year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟誼漶由紫陽王嗣。

translations.literal: He had no son; his younger brother Yihuan succeeded from the title Prince of Ziyang.
translations.idiomatic: Without a son, his younger brother Yihuan succeeded from the rank of Prince of Ziyang.

sentences.zh: 薨，子存樞嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Cunshu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and his son Cunshu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 李自成破西安，存樞降於賊，偽授權將軍，妃劉氏死之。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng took Xi'an, Cunshu surrendered to the rebels and was falsely appointed General of Authority; Consort Liu died for her integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng captured Xi'an, Cunshu submitted to the rebels and accepted a bogus rank as General of Authority; Consort Liu took her own life.

sentences.zh: 汧陽王誠洌，康王諸孫也，事父及繼母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Prince of Qianyang Zhu Chenglie, a grandson of Prince Kang, was known for serving his father and stepmother with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Chenglie, Prince of Qianyang, a grandson of Prince Kang, was famed for his filial care of his father and stepmother.

sentences.zh: 父疾，經月不解帶。

translations.literal: When his father fell ill, for a full month he did not loosen his belt.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill, he went a full month without loosening his belt in attendance.

sentences.zh: 及薨，醯醬鹽酪不入口。

translations.literal: When his father died, he took no vinegar, sauce, salt, or cheese into his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he refused all seasoned food, eating only the plainest fare.

sentences.zh: 明年，墓生嘉禾，一本雙穗，嘉瓜二實並蒂，慈烏異鳥環集。

translations.literal: The next year at the tomb grew fine grain with one stalk and two ears, fine melons with two fruits on one stem, and filial crows and strange birds gathered all around.
translations.idiomatic: The following year fine grain with twin ears and melons with conjoined fruit appeared at the tomb, and filial crows and rare birds gathered there.

sentences.zh: 以母馬妃早卒，不逮養，追服衰食蔬者三年。

translations.literal: Because his mother, Consort Ma, had died early and he had been unable to support her, he observed mourning garments and ate vegetables for three years in retrospective filial service.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother, Lady Ma, had died while he was young and he had never been able to care for her, he wore mourning and ate only vegetables for three years in belated filial observance.

sentences.zh: 雪中萱草生華，鹹謂孝感所致。

translations.literal: Daylilies bloomed in the snow, and all said this was caused by the moving power of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Daylilies blossomed in the snow, and all took it as a sign of filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年賜敕嘉獎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi an edict of commendation was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 15 the throne issued an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 時有輔國將軍秉樺，亦好學篤行。

translations.literal: At the time there was also Supporter-General of the State Zhu Binghua, who likewise loved learning and practiced earnest conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Supporter-General Zhu Binghua was also known for scholarship and upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 父病，禱於神，乞以身代，疾竟愈。

translations.literal: When his father fell ill, he prayed to the spirits, begging to take the illness upon himself, and the sickness was finally cured.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill, he prayed to the gods to suffer in his father's place, and the illness lifted.

sentences.zh: 母喪廬墓，有雙鶴集庭中。

translations.literal: At his mother's death he built a hut by the tomb, and a pair of cranes gathered in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his mother in a hut beside her tomb, and a pair of cranes appeared in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 定王以聞。

translations.literal: Prince Ding reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ding Zhu Jixi reported the matter to the court.

sentences.zh: 世宗表其門。

translations.literal: The Shizong emperor honored his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiajing Emperor bestowed a commemorative plaque upon his gate.

sentences.zh: 晉恭王□，太祖第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Gong of Jin Zhu □ was the third son of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu □, Prince Gong of Jin, was the Hongwu Emperor's third son.

sentences.zh: 學文於宋濂，學書於杜環，洪武三年封。

translations.literal: He studied literature with Song Lian and calligraphy with Du Huan, and was enfeoffed in the third year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He studied letters under Song Lian and calligraphy under Du Huan, and received his enfeoffment in Hongwu 3.

sentences.zh: 十一年就籓太原，中道笞膳夫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he went to his fief at Taiyuan and on the way flogged a steward.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he took up residence at his fief in Taiyuan and, en route, had a kitchen steward beaten.

sentences.zh: 帝馳諭曰：「吾帥群英平禍亂，不為姑息。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an urgent message, saying: "I led the heroes to pacify turmoil and do not show indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a swift reprimand: "I led the realm's finest men to quell chaos—I do not coddle wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 獨膳夫徐興祖，事吾二十三年未嘗折辱。

translations.literal: Only the steward Xu Xingzu, who served me twenty-three years without once being humiliated—
translations.idiomatic: Only Xu Xingzu, my kitchen steward, has served me twenty-three years without once suffering insult—

sentences.zh: 怨不在大，小子識之。」

translations.literal: resentment does not lie in great things; remember this, boy.
translations.idiomatic: grievance need not be great to endure. Mark this well, boy.

sentences.zh: □修目美髯，顧盼有威，多智數。

translations.literal: Zhu □ had fine eyes and a handsome beard, was imposing in glance, and was full of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu □ had striking eyes and a fine beard, a commanding presence, and a shrewd mind.

sentences.zh: 然性驕，在國多不法。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was arrogant and in his domain committed many illegal acts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was proud by nature and committed many unlawful acts within his domain.

sentences.zh: 或告棡有異謀。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Zhu □ harbored treasonous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Someone denounced Zhu □ for plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，欲罪之，太子力救得免。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and wished to punish him; the heir apparent strongly interceded and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and meant to punish him, but the crown prince pleaded strenuously and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，太子巡陝西歸，□岡隨來朝，敕歸籓。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the crown prince returned from inspecting Shaanxi; Zhu □Gang followed him to court and was ordered to return to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 24 the crown prince returned from inspecting Shaanxi; Zhu □Gang accompanied him to court and was ordered back to his fief.

sentences.zh: 自是折節，待官屬皆有禮，更以恭慎聞。

translations.literal: From then on he restrained himself, treated his officials with courtesy, and became known for respectful prudence.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he mended his ways, treated his staff with courtesy, and came to be known for humble discretion.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝念邊防甚，且欲諸子習兵事，諸王封並塞居者皆預軍務。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was deeply concerned about frontier defense and wished his sons to learn military affairs; all princes enfeoffed along the border participated in military duties.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was keenly anxious about the frontier and wanted his sons trained in warfare; every prince enfeoffed along the northern marches took part in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 而晉、燕二王，尤被重寄，數命將兵出塞及築城屯田。

translations.literal: The princes of Jin and Yan in particular were entrusted with heavy responsibility and were repeatedly ordered to lead troops beyond the passes, build fortifications, and open military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Jin and Yan bore the heaviest trust, repeatedly ordered to command troops beyond the frontier, build walled posts, and open garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 大將如宋國公馮勝、穎國公傅友德皆受節制。

translations.literal: Great generals such as Duke of Song Feng Sheng and Duke of Ying Fu Youde were all placed under their command.
translations.idiomatic: Field commanders of the highest rank, such as Feng Sheng, Duke of Song, and Fu Youde, Duke of Ying, all served under their orders.

sentences.zh: 又詔二王，軍中事大者方以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor also instructed the two princes that only major military matters need be reported.
translations.idiomatic: He further instructed the two princes to report to the throne only on weighty military matters.

sentences.zh: 三十一年三月薨，子定王濟熹嗣。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-first year he died; his son Prince Ding Zhu Jixi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of year thirty-one; his son Zhu Jixi, Prince Ding, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，帝以濟熹縱下，黜其長史龍潭。

translations.literal: Early in Yongle the emperor, because Jixi was lax with subordinates, dismissed his chief steward Long Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign the emperor, finding Jixi indulgent toward his staff, dismissed his chief steward Long Tan.

sentences.zh: 濟熹懼，欲上護衛。

translations.literal: Jixi was afraid and wished to surrender his guard units to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Jixi grew fearful and offered to turn his guard regiments over to the court.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: Permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: The request was refused.

sentences.zh: 弟平陽王濟熿，幼狠戾，失愛於父。

translations.literal: His younger brother, Prince of Pingyang Zhu Jihuang, was cruel and violent from childhood and unloved by his father.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhu Jihuang, Prince of Pingyang, had been fierce and unruly since boyhood and had lost his father's favor.

sentences.zh: 及長，太祖召秦、晉、燕、週四世子及庶子之長者，教於京師。

translations.literal: When he grew up, Taizu summoned the heir apparents of Qin, Jin, Yan, and Zhou and the eldest sons among the secondary sons to be instructed at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, Taizu summoned the heir apparents of Qin, Jin, Yan, and Zhou, together with the eldest sons among the lesser princes, to be educated at the capital.

sentences.zh: 濟熿與燕王子高煦、周王子有□動邪詭相比，不為太祖所愛。

translations.literal: Jihuang associated with Zhu Gaoxu, son of the Prince of Yan, and Zhu You□ of Zhou in mischief and crafty schemes, and was not loved by Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Jihuang kept company with Zhu Gaoxu of Yan and Zhu You□ of Zhou in roguery and deceit, and won no affection from Taizu.

sentences.zh: 濟熹既嗣王，成祖封濟熿平陽王。

translations.literal: After Jixi succeeded as prince, Chengzu enfeoffed Jihuang as Prince of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jixi had succeeded to the princedom, the Yongle Emperor enfeoffed Jihuang as Prince of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 濟熿追憾父，並憾濟熹不為解，嗾其弟慶成王濟炫等日訴濟熹過於朝，又誘府中官校，文致其罪，歷年不已。

translations.literal: Jihuang bore lasting resentment toward his father and also resented that Jixi did not plead on his behalf; he incited his younger brothers, including Prince of Qingcheng Zhu Jixuan, to denounce Jixi's faults at court daily, and seduced officers of the princely establishment to fabricate charges against him, year after year without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Jihuang brooded over his father's disfavor and blamed Jixi for not interceding; he urged his younger brothers, including Zhu Jixuan, Prince of Qingcheng, to denounce Jixi at court day after day, and suborned officers of the princely household to frame charges against him, year on year without end.

sentences.zh: 十二年，帝奪濟熹爵，及世子美圭皆為庶人，俾守恭王園，而立濟熿為晉王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor stripped Jixi of his rank; Jixi and his heir apparent Meigui were both made commoners and ordered to guard Prince Gong's mausoleum grove, while Jihuang was installed as Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve the emperor deprived Jixi of his title; Jixi and his heir Zhu Meigui were reduced to commoners and set to guard Prince Gong's tomb park, while Jihuang was raised up as Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 濟熿既立，益橫暴，至進毒弒嫡母謝氏，逼烝恭王侍兒吉祥，幽濟熹父子，蔬食不給。

translations.literal: Once established, Jihuang grew ever more violent; he even administered poison to murder his stepmother Lady Xie, forced himself on Prince Gong's attendant Ji'xiang, imprisoned Jixi and his son, and gave them only vegetables without adequate supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned in the princedom, Jihuang grew still more brutal: he poisoned his stepmother Lady Xie, violated Prince Gong's attendant Ji'xiang, and shut Jixi and his son in confinement on a meager vegetarian ration.

sentences.zh: 父兄故侍從宮人多為所害，莫敢言。

translations.literal: Many former attendants and palace women of his father and elder brother were harmed by him, and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his father's and elder brother's former attendants and palace women fell victim to him, and none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 恭王宮中老媼走訴成祖，乃即獄中召晉府故承奉左微問之，盡得濟熿構濟熹狀。

translations.literal: An old woman of Prince Gong's palace fled to report to Chengzu, who immediately summoned from prison the former attendant of the Jin establishment Zuo Wei and questioned him, learning in full how Jihuang had framed Jixi.
translations.idiomatic: An old serving woman of Prince Gong's household escaped to inform the Yongle Emperor, who at once summoned from prison Zuo Wei, a former attendant of the Jin establishment, and learned the full story of Jihuang's plot against Jixi.

sentences.zh: 立命微馳召濟熹父子，濟熹幽空室已十年矣。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered Wei to gallop and summon Jixi and his son; Jixi had been imprisoned in an empty room for ten years already.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered Wei to ride posthaste and summon Jixi and his son—Jixi had languished ten years in an empty cell.

sentences.zh: 左微者，故因濟熹牽連繫獄，或傳微死已久。

translations.literal: Zuo Wei had been imprisoned because of connection with Jixi, and some said Wei had long been dead.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Wei had been imprisoned on Jixi's account, and rumor held that he had died long before.

sentences.zh: 及至，一府大驚。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the entire princely establishment was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: When he appeared, the whole princely household was thunderstruck.

sentences.zh: 微入空室，釋濟熹父子，相抱持大慟。

translations.literal: Wei entered the empty room, released Jixi and his son, and they embraced and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Wei entered the empty cell, freed Jixi and his son, and the three embraced and wailed together.

sentences.zh: 時帝北征，駐驛沙城，濟□喜父子謁行在所。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was on a northern campaign, encamped at Shacheng; Zhu Ji□ and his son came to the mobile palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then on campaign in the north, halted at Shacheng; Zhu Ji□ and his son presented themselves at the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 帝見濟熹病，惻然，封美圭平陽王，使奉父居平陽，予以恭王故連伯灘田。

translations.literal: Seeing Jixi ill, the emperor was moved with compassion; he enfeoffed Meigui as Prince of Pingyang and had him support his father at Pingyang, granting fields on the former Jin estates at Lianbotan.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Jixi wasted by illness, the emperor was moved to pity; he enfeoffed Meigui as Prince of Pingyang to attend his father there and granted him the former Jin estates at Lianbotan.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，濟熿遂不與美圭田。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Jihuang then refused to grant Meigui the fields.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Jihuang refused to hand over the allotted fields to Meigui.

sentences.zh: 仁宗連以書諭，卒不聽。

translations.literal: Renzong repeatedly sent letters instructing him, but in the end he would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongxi Emperor wrote again and again to admonish him, yet in the end he would not comply.

sentences.zh: 又聞朝廷賜濟熹王者冠服及他賚予，益怨望。

translations.literal: When he also heard that the court had bestowed princely robes and other gifts upon Jixi, his resentment grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Learning moreover that the court had granted Jixi princely regalia and other gifts, his resentment only deepened.

sentences.zh: 成祖、仁宗之崩，不為服，使寺人代臨，幕中廣致妖巫為詛咒不輟。

translations.literal: At the deaths of Chengzu and Renzong he wore no mourning; he had eunuchs attend in his stead, and within his screen-tent he repeatedly summoned sorcerers to curse without cease.
translations.idiomatic: At the deaths of Yongle and Hongxi he wore no mourning, sending eunuchs to stand in for him, while within his pavilion he constantly brought in sorcerers to work curses.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，濟熿密遣人結高煦謀不軌，寧化王濟煥告變。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, Jihuang secretly sent men to join with Gaoxu in plotting rebellion; Prince of Ninghua Zhu Jihuan reported the conspiracy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuande Emperor took the throne, Jihuang secretly sent agents to conspire with Zhu Gaoxu; Zhu Jihuan, Prince of Ninghua, reported the plot.

sentences.zh: 比擒高煦，又得濟熿交通書，帝未之問也，而濟熿所遣使高煦人懼罪及，走京師首實。

translations.literal: When Gaoxu was captured, letters showing Jihuang's communications were also obtained; the emperor had not yet questioned him, but the envoy Jihuang had sent to Gaoxu's camp, fearing implication, fled to the capital and confessed the facts.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaoxu was taken, correspondence linking Jihuang to him was also found; the emperor had not yet moved against Jihuang, but the messenger Jihuang had sent to Gaoxu's camp, fearing guilt by association, fled to the capital and confessed everything.

sentences.zh: 內使劉信等數十人告濟熿擅取屯糧十萬餘石，欲應高煦，並發其宮中詛咒事。

translations.literal: Inner attendants Liu Xin and several dozen others reported that Jihuang had appropriated more than a hundred thousand shi of garrison grain intending to support Gaoxu, and also exposed the cursing rites within his palace.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Liu Xin and several dozen others reported that Jihuang had seized more than a hundred thousand shi of garrison grain to aid Gaoxu, and also exposed the curse rites within his palace.

sentences.zh: 濟煥亦至是始知嫡母被弒，馳奏。

translations.literal: Jihuan only then learned that his stepmother had been murdered and raced to memorialize the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Jihuan learn that his stepmother had been murdered, and he rushed a memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 遣人察實，召至京，示以諸所發奸逆狀，廢為庶人，幽鳳陽。

translations.literal: The court sent men to verify the facts, summoned him to the capital, showed him all the revealed treacherous acts, degraded him to commoner status, and imprisoned him at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent investigators to verify the charges, summoned him to the capital, confronted him with every act of treachery that had come to light, stripped him to commoner rank, and immured him at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 同謀官屬及諸巫悉論死。

translations.literal: Co-conspirators among his officials and all the sorcerers were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: His accomplices among the staff and all the sorcerers were condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 時宣德二年四月也。

translations.literal: This was in the fourth month of Xuande year two.
translations.idiomatic: This took place in the fourth month of Xuande 2.

sentences.zh: 晉國絕封凡八年，至英宗即位之二月，乃進封美圭為晉王，還居太原。

translations.literal: The Jin line was extinct for eight years in all; in the second month after Yingzong's accession Meigui was advanced to Prince of Jin and returned to dwell at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin princedom lay vacant eight years in all; in the second month after the Yingzong Emperor's accession, Meigui was restored as Prince of Jin and returned to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 正統六年薨。

translations.literal: He died in Zhengtong year six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhengtong 6.

sentences.zh: 子莊王鐘鉉嗣，弘治十五年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Zhuang Zhu Zhongxuan succeeded and died in Hongzhi year fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Zhongxuan, Prince Zhuang, succeeded him and died in Hongzhi 15.

sentences.zh: 世子奇源及其子表榮皆前卒，表榮子端王知烊嗣。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Qiyuan and his son Biaorong both predeceased him; Biaorong's son Prince Duan Zhu Zhiyang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent Qiyuan and his son Biaorong had both died earlier; Biaorong's son Zhu Zhiyang, Prince Duan, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 知烊七歲而孤，能盡哀，居母喪嘔血，芝生寢宮。

translations.literal: Zhiyang was orphaned at seven, showed full filial grief, vomited blood during mourning for his mother, and lingzhi fungus grew in his bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyang lost his father at seven, yet mourned with full devotion; during his mother's funeral he vomited blood, and lingzhi fungus sprang up in his sleeping quarters.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十二年薨。

translations.literal: He died in Jiajing year twelve.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiajing 12.

sentences.zh: 無子，再從子簡王新□典嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, a collateral descendant Prince Jian Zhu Xin□dian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; a great-grandnephew, Zhu Xin□dian, Prince Jian, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 新化王表槏、滎澤王表□者，端王諸父也。

translations.literal: Prince of Xinhua Zhu Biaoqiao and Prince of Rongze Zhu Biao□ were paternal uncles of Prince Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Biaoqiao, Prince of Xinhua, and Zhu Biao□, Prince of Rongze, were Prince Duan's uncles.

sentences.zh: 表槏先卒，子知 □節嗣為新化王，亦前卒，二子新□典、新橋。

translations.literal: Biaoqiao died first; his son Zhu Zhi□jie succeeded as Prince of Xinhua, also predeceased; two sons, Xin□dian and Xinqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Biaoqiao died first; his son Zhu Zhi□jie succeeded as Prince of Xinhua but also predeceased him, leaving two sons, Xin□dian and Xinqiao.

sentences.zh: 端王請新□典嗣新化王，未封而端王薨，表□謀攝府事。

translations.literal: Prince Duan requested Xin□dian to succeed as Prince of Xinhua; before the enfeoffment Prince Duan died, and Biao□ plotted to take charge of the establishment affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Duan petitioned that Xin□dian succeed as Prince of Xinhua; before the patent was issued Prince Duan died, and Biao□ schemed to seize control of the princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 端王妃王氏曰：「王無後，次及新化王，新化父子卒，有孫新□典在。」

translations.literal: Princess consort of Duan Lady Wang said: "The prince has no heir; next in line is the Prince of Xinhua; father and son of Xinhua are deceased, but a grandson Xin□dian survives.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Duan's consort, Lady Wang, said: "The prince has no heir; succession passes next to the Prince of Xinhua; both father and son of that line are dead, but a grandson, Xin□dian, remains.

sentences.zh: 即召入府，拜几筵為喪主。

translations.literal: She immediately summoned him into the palace, and he bowed before the spirit tablet as chief mourner.
translations.idiomatic: She summoned him into the palace at once, and he bowed before the spirit tablet as chief mourner.

sentences.zh: 表□忿曰：「我尊行，顧不得王。」

translations.literal: Biao□ said angrily: "I am the senior line—how can I not receive the princedom?
translations.idiomatic: Biao□ protested in anger: "I am the senior line—am I to be passed over for the title?

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「新□典故新化王長子，不得為人後，新□典宜嗣新化王，新橋宜嗣晉王。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Xin□dian is the eldest son of the former Prince of Xinhua and cannot become another man's heir; Xin□dian ought to succeed Xinhua, and Xinqiao ought to succeed Jin."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "Xin□dian, as eldest son of the late Prince of Xinhua, cannot be adopted as another man's heir; Xin□dian should succeed Xinhua, and Xinqiao should succeed Jin."

sentences.zh: 禮部議新□典宜嗣，是為簡王。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites decided Xin□dian should succeed, and he became Prince Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites ruled that Xin□dian should succeed, and he became Prince Jian.

sentences.zh: 新□典母太妃尚氏嚴，教子以禮。

translations.literal: Xin□dian's mother Grand Consort Lady Shang was strict and taught her son by ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Xin□dian's mother, Grand Consort Lady Shang, was severe and reared her son in ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 太妃疾，新□典叩頭露禱。

translations.literal: When the Grand Consort fell ill, Xin□dian knocked his head bareheaded in open prayer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Consort fell ill, Xin□dian prayed bareheaded in the open air, knocking his forehead to the ground.

sentences.zh: 長史有敷陳，輒拜受教。

translations.literal: When the chief steward offered admonitions, he always bowed and accepted instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his chief steward offered counsel, he bowed and accepted the lesson.

sentences.zh: 其老也，以弟鎮國將軍新橋子慎鏡攝籓事。

translations.literal: In his old age he had his younger brother's son, Defender-General of the State Shenjing, son of Xinqiao, administer fief affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he had his younger brother's son Zhu Shenjing, Defender-General of the State and son of Xinqiao, administer the fief in his stead.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三年薨，慎鏡亦卒。

translations.literal: In Wanli year three he died; Shenjing also died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Wanli 3; Shenjing died as well.

sentences.zh: 弟惠王慎鋷嗣，七年薨。

translations.literal: His younger brother Prince Hui Zhu Shenchou succeeded and died in year seven.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhu Shenchou, Prince Hui, succeeded him and died in year seven.

sentences.zh: 子穆王敏淳嗣，三十八年薨，子求桂嗣。

translations.literal: His son Prince Mu Zhu Minchun succeeded; in year thirty-eight he died, and his son Qiugui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Minchun, Prince Mu, succeeded; he died in year thirty-eight, and his son Qiugui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 李自成陷山西，求桂與秦王存樞並為賊所執，入北京，不知所終。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng seized Shanxi, Qiugui and Prince of Qin Cunshu were both seized by the bandits, taken to Beijing, and their ultimate fate is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng overran Shanxi, Qiugui and Zhu Cunshu of Qin were both seized by the rebels and carried to Beijing; their ultimate fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 西河王奇溯，定王曾孫。

translations.literal: Prince of Xihe Zhu Qisuo was a great-grandson of Prince Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qisuo, Prince of Xihe, was a great-grandson of Prince Ding.

sentences.zh: 三歲而孤。

translations.literal: He was orphaned at three.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at the age of three.

sentences.zh: 問父所在，即慟哭。

translations.literal: When he asked where his father was, he would burst into tears.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he asked where his father was, he would burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 長，刻栴檀為父順簡王像，祀之。

translations.literal: When grown, he carved a sandalwood image of his father Prince Jian of Shun and worshipped it.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he carved a sandalwood image of his father, Prince Jian of Shun, and made offerings to it.

sentences.zh: 母病渴，中夜稽顙禱天，俄有甘泉自地湧出。

translations.literal: When his mother suffered thirst, at midnight he knocked his forehead praying to Heaven, and presently sweet spring water gushed from the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was parched with thirst, he prayed at midnight, knocking his forehead to the earth, and presently a sweet spring welled up from the ground.

sentences.zh: 母飲泉，病良已。

translations.literal: His mother drank the spring and her illness was fully cured.
translations.idiomatic: His mother drank from the spring and was fully restored to health.

sentences.zh: 及卒，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: At her death his grief left him emaciated as a skeleton.
translations.idiomatic: At her death his mourning left him wasted to the bone.

sentences.zh: 子表相嗣，亦以仁孝聞，與寧河王表楠、河東嗣王奇淮並為人所稱。

translations.literal: His son Biaoxiang succeeded, likewise famed for benevolence and filial piety, and together with Prince of Ninghe Biaonan and heir to Prince of Hedong Qihuai was praised by all.
translations.idiomatic: His son Biaoxiang succeeded him, likewise famed for benevolence and filial devotion; he, Zhu Biaonan of Ninghe, and Zhu Qihuai, heir to the Prince of Hedong, were all widely praised.

sentences.zh: 新堞，恭王七世孫，家汾州。

translations.literal: Xinlie was a seventh-generation descendant of Prince Gong and lived at Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xinlie, a seventh-generation descendant of Prince Gong, made his home at Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十四年由宗貢生為中部知縣。

translations.literal: In Chongzhen year fourteen he passed the metropolitan examination through the imperial clan quota and became magistrate of Zhongbu county.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 14 he passed the metropolitan examination through the imperial-clan quota and was appointed magistrate of Zhongbu County.

sentences.zh: 有事他邑，土寇乘間陷其城，坐免官。

translations.literal: While on business elsewhere, bandits took advantage of the interval to seize the county seat, and he was dismissed from office as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: While away on official business, local bandits seized the chance to overrun the county seat, and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 已而復任。

translations.literal: Later he was reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reappointed to the post.

sentences.zh: 署事者聞賊且至，亟欲解印去，新堞毅然曰：「此我致命之秋也。」

translations.literal: The acting official heard the rebels were about to arrive and urgently wished to surrender the seal and leave; Xinlie said resolutely: "This is the season in which I must give my life.
translations.idiomatic: The acting magistrate heard the rebels were near and was eager to hand over the seal and flee; Xinlie said firmly: "This is the hour in which I must lay down my life.

sentences.zh: 即受之。

translations.literal: He immediately accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He took the seal at once.

sentences.zh: 得賊所傳偽檄，怒而碎之，議拒守。

translations.literal: Obtaining the rebels' forged proclamation, he angrily tore it to pieces and deliberated on resisting and holding the city.
translations.idiomatic: When he received the rebels' forged summons, he tore it to shreds in anger and resolved to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 邑新遭寇，無應者，乃屬父老速去，而己誓必死。

translations.literal: The district had just suffered bandit raids and none would respond; he entrusted the elders to flee quickly while he himself vowed he must die.
translations.idiomatic: The county had just been ravaged by bandits and none would answer his call; he urged the elders to flee at once while he himself swore to die.

sentences.zh: 妻盧氏，妾薛氏、馮氏，請先死。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Lu, concubines Lady Xue and Lady Feng, asked to die first.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Lu and his concubines Lady Xue and Lady Feng asked to die before him.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: He granted their request.
translations.idiomatic: He consented.

sentences.zh: 有女數歲，拊其背而勉之縊。

translations.literal: He had a daughter several years old; patting her back he urged her to hang herself.
translations.idiomatic: He had a daughter of several years; stroking her back, he urged her to hang herself.

sentences.zh: 左右皆泣下。

translations.literal: Those around him all wept.
translations.idiomatic: All who were present wept.

sentences.zh: 乃書表封印，使人馳送京師，冠帶望闕拜，又望拜其母，遂自經。

translations.literal: He wrote a petition, sealed it, and had a man gallop to deliver it to the capital; wearing cap and belt he bowed toward the palace gate, bowed again toward his mother, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a memorial, sealed it, and sent a rider posthaste to the capital; then, in full cap and robes, he bowed toward the palace gate, bowed again toward his mother's direction, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 士民葬之社壇側，以妻女祔。

translations.literal: The gentlemen and commoners buried him beside the altar of the soil god, with his wife and daughter apportioned beside him.
translations.idiomatic: The local gentry and commoners buried him beside the altar of the soil god, with his wife and daughter laid to rest beside him.

sentences.zh: 先是，土寇薄城，縣丞光先與戰不勝，自焚死。

translations.literal: Earlier, when bandits pressed the city, Assistant Magistrate Guangxian fought them without victory and burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when bandits threatened the walls, the assistant magistrate Guangxian fought them without success and burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 新堞哭之慟，為之誄曰：「殺身成仁，雖死猶生。」

translations.literal: Xinlie wept bitterly for him and composed an elegy saying: "To give one's body for benevolence—though dead, one lives on.
translations.idiomatic: Xinlie mourned him bitterly and wrote an elegy: "He gave his life for humaneness—though dead, he lives on.

sentences.zh: 至是，新堞亦死難。

translations.literal: Now Xinlie too died a martyr's death.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xinlie, too, died a martyr's death.

sentences.zh: 周定王橚，太祖第五子。

translations.literal: Prince Ding of Zhou Zhu Su was the fifth son of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Su, Prince Ding of Zhou, was the Hongwu Emperor's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年封吳王。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year three he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 七年，有司請置護衛於杭州。

translations.literal: In year seven the relevant offices requested establishing a guard at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven the responsible offices petitioned to station a guard detachment at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「錢塘財賦地，不可。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Qiantang is a land of fiscal revenue; that will not do."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Qiantang is the empire's revenue heartland—that will not do.

sentences.zh: 十一年改封周王，命與燕、楚、齊三王駐鳳陽。

translations.literal: In year eleven his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Zhou, and he was ordered to reside at Fengyang together with the princes of Yan, Chu, and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Zhou and ordered to take up residence at Fengyang alongside the princes of Yan, Chu, and Qi.

sentences.zh: 十四年就籓開封，即宋故宮地為府。

translations.literal: In year fourteen he went to his fief at Kaifeng, making the site of the Song imperial palace his princely seat.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he entered his fief at Kaifeng and established his government on the ground of the former Song palace.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，橚棄其國來鳳陽。

translations.literal: In year twenty-two, Su abandoned his domain and came to Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two Zhu Su left his fief and returned to Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，將徙之雲南，尋止，使居京師，世子有燉理籓事。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and was about to relocate him to Yunnan; he soon stopped, had him live in the capital, and the heir Zhu Youdun handled fief affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and was about to banish him to Yunnan, but soon relented, kept him in the capital, and had the heir Zhu Youdun administer the fief.

sentences.zh: 二十四年十二月敕歸籓。

translations.literal: In year twenty-four, twelfth month, an edict ordered him to return to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year twenty-four he was commanded to return to his fief.

sentences.zh: 建文初，以橚燕王母弟，頗疑憚之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign, because Su was the younger brother of the Prince of Yan's mother, the court greatly suspected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwen reign, because Zhu Su was uterine brother to the Prince of Yan, the court viewed him with deep suspicion and dread.

sentences.zh: 橚亦時有異謀，長史王翰數諫不納，佯狂去。

translations.literal: Su also at times harbored irregular designs; Chief Steward Wang Han repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded and feigned madness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Su too nursed occasional disloyal schemes; his chief steward Wang Han remonstrated again and again without being heeded and finally feigned madness and departed.

sentences.zh: □肅次子汝南王有□動告變。

translations.literal: □Su's second son, the Prince of Runan Zhu You□, stirred a report of treason.
translations.idiomatic: □Su's second son, the Prince of Runan Zhu You□, set in motion a denunciation of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝使李景隆備邊，道出汴，猝圍王宮，執橚，竄蒙化，諸子並別徙。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Li Jinglong to guard the frontier; his route passed Bian, where he suddenly surrounded the princely palace, seized Su, who fled to Menghua, and all his sons were separately relocated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Li Jinglong to secure the border; passing Bian on the way, he suddenly besieged the princely palace, seized Zhu Su—who fled to Menghua—and sent all his sons into separate exile.

sentences.zh: 已，復召還京，錮之。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was again summoned back to the capital and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recalled to the capital again and placed under confinement.

sentences.zh: 成祖入南京，復爵，加祿五千石。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor entered Nanjing, his rank was restored and his stipend increased by five thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongle Emperor entered Nanjing, Zhu Su's title was restored and his grain stipend was raised by five thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年正月詔歸其舊封，獻頌九章及佾舞。

translations.literal: In the first month of Yongle year one an edict returned his former fief; he presented nine eulogies and yayue dance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yongle 1 he was ordered back to his old fief and presented nine laudatory odes together with court ceremonial dance.

sentences.zh: 明年來朝，獻騶虞。

translations.literal: The next year he came to court and presented a zouyu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he attended court and offered a zouyu.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，宴賜甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and feasted and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and entertained and rewarded him with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 以汴梁有河患，將改封洛陽。

translations.literal: Because Bianliang suffered from river calamities, the court was about to change his fief to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Bianliang was afflicted by flooding, the court planned to transfer his fief to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 橚言汴堤固，無重勞民力。

translations.literal: Su said the Bian embankments were solid and there was no need to heavily burden the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Su argued that the Bian dikes were secure and that the people should not be put to great trouble again.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The plan was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 十四年疏辭所賜在城稅課。

translations.literal: In year fourteen he memorialized declining the in-city tax levies he had been granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he submitted a memorial declining the urban tax franchises he had been granted.

sentences.zh: 十八年十月有告橚反者。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of year eighteen someone reported that Su was rebelling.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year eighteen a report accused Zhu Su of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝察之有驗。

translations.literal: The emperor investigated and found evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked into the matter and found it substantiated.

sentences.zh: 明年二月召至京，示以所告詞。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year he was summoned to the capital and shown the words of the accusation.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he was summoned to the capital and confronted with the denunciation.

sentences.zh: 橚頓首謝死罪。

translations.literal: Su knocked his head to the ground and begged forgiveness for a capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Su prostrated himself and pleaded guilty of a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 帝憐之，不復問。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him and did not pursue the matter further.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on him and let the affair drop.

sentences.zh: 橚歸國，獻還三護衛。

translations.literal: Su returned to his domain and submitted back the three guard corps.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Su returned to his fief and handed back his three guard detachments.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，加歲祿至二萬石。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor acceded, his annual stipend was raised to twenty thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor came to the throne, his yearly stipend was increased to twenty thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 橚好學，能詞賦，嘗作《元宮詞》百章。

translations.literal: Su loved learning and could compose lyrics; he once wrote one hundred chapters of Yuan Palace Lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Su was devoted to learning and skilled in regulated verse; he once composed one hundred chapters of Yuan Palace Lyrics.

sentences.zh: 以國土夷曠，庶草蕃廡，考核其可佐饑饉者四百餘種，繪圖疏之，名《救荒本草》。

translations.literal: Because the state's lands were broad and level and many grasses flourished, he examined more than four hundred kinds that could aid famine relief, drew pictures and memorialized them, and titled the work Famine-Relief Materia Medica.
translations.idiomatic: As his domain was wide and flat and wild plants grew in profusion, he catalogued more than four hundred species useful against famine, illustrated them in a memorial, and entitled the work Famine-Relief Materia Medica.

sentences.zh: 辟東書堂以教世子，長史劉淳為之師。

translations.literal: He opened the Eastern Study Hall to instruct the heir, with Chief Steward Liu Chun as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Eastern Study Hall to educate the heir apparent, appointing Chief Steward Liu Chun as instructor.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年薨。

translations.literal: In Hongxi year one he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Hongxi 1.

sentences.zh: 弟簡王有爝嗣，景泰三年薨。

translations.literal: His younger brother Prince Jian Zhu Youjiao succeeded; in Jingtai year three he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was succeeded by his younger brother Zhu Youjiao, Prince Jian, who died in Jingtai 3.

sentences.zh: 子靖王子垕嗣，七年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Jing Zhu Ziheng succeeded; in year seven he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Ziheng, Prince Jing, succeeded and died in year seven.

sentences.zh: 弟懿王子驩嗣，成化二十一年薨。

translations.literal: His younger brother Prince Yi Zhu Zihuan succeeded; in Chenghua year twenty-one he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was succeeded by his younger brother Zhu Zihuan, Prince Yi, who died in Chenghua 21.

sentences.zh: 子惠王同鑣嗣，弘治十一年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Hui Zhu Tongbiao succeeded; in Hongzhi year eleven he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Tongbiao, Prince Hui, succeeded and died in Hongzhi 11.

sentences.zh: 世子安水橫未襲封而卒，孫恭王睦□審嗣，謚安水橫悼王。

translations.literal: The heir An Shuiheng died before inheriting the fief; the grandson Prince Gong Zhu Mu□shen succeeded, and An Shuiheng was posthumously titled Prince Dao.
translations.idiomatic: The heir An Shuiheng died before taking the fief; his grandson Zhu Mu□shen, Prince Gong, succeeded, and An Shuiheng was given the posthumous title Prince Dao.

sentences.zh: 初，安水橫為世子，與弟平樂王安泛、義寧王安水矣爭漁利，置囹圄刑具，集亡賴為私人。

translations.literal: Initially, when An Shuiheng was heir, he and his younger brothers the Prince of Pingle Zhu Anfan and the Prince of Yining Zhu An Shuiyi fought over fishing profits, set up prisons and torture instruments, and gathered desperadoes as private retainers.
translations.idiomatic: At first, while An Shuiheng was heir apparent, he and his younger brothers Zhu Anfan, Prince of Pingle, and Zhu An Shuiyi, Prince of Yining, fought over fishing rights, established dungeons and penal gear, and recruited ruffians as personal followers.

sentences.zh: 惠王戒安水橫，不從，王怒。

translations.literal: Prince Hui admonished An Shuiheng, but he would not obey, and the prince was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui warned An Shuiheng, but he refused to listen, and the prince grew furious.

sentences.zh: 安泛因而傾之，安水橫亦持安泛不法事。

translations.literal: Anfan therefore undermined him, while An Shuiheng also held evidence of Anfan's unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Anfan in turn worked to destroy him, while An Shuiheng also gathered proof of Anfan's illegal acts.

sentences.zh: 惠王薨，群小交構，安水橫奏安泛私壞社稷壇，營私第，安泛亦誣奏安水橫諸陰事。

translations.literal: When Prince Hui died, petty men mutually incited strife; An Shuiheng reported that Anfan had privately destroyed the altar of soil and grain and built a private residence, while Anfan also falsely reported An Shuiheng's secret deeds.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Hui's death, schemers played them against one another: An Shuiheng accused Anfan of privately damaging the state altar and building a private mansion, while Anfan in turn slandered An Shuiheng with hidden crimes.

sentences.zh: 下鎮、巡官按驗。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to garrison and touring officials for verification.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to garrison and circuit investigators for examination.

sentences.zh: 頃之，安水橫死，其子睦□審立而幼。

translations.literal: Before long An Shuiheng died; his son Zhu Mu□shen was established but was still young.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward An Shuiheng died, leaving his son Zhu Mu□shen as heir while still a minor.

sentences.zh: 安泛侵陵世子妃，安涘亦訐妃出不正，其子不可嗣。

translations.literal: Anfan encroached upon the heir's consort; An Si also impeached the consort for improper birth, saying her son could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Anfan harassed the heir's consort, while An Si also charged that the consort's origins were illegitimate and that her son was unfit to inherit.

sentences.zh: 十三年，帝命太監魏忠、刑部侍郎何鑒按治。

translations.literal: In year thirteen the emperor ordered the eunuch Wei Zhong and Vice Minister of Justice He Jian to investigate and settle the case.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen the emperor appointed the eunuch Wei Zhong and Vice Minister of Justice He Jian to conduct a full inquiry.

sentences.zh: 安泛懼，益誣世子毒殺惠王並世子妃淫亂，所連逮千人。

translations.literal: Anfan grew afraid and further falsely accused the heir of poisoning Prince Hui and of the consort's lewd disorder; more than a thousand persons were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Anfan escalated his charges, falsely claiming the heir had poisoned Prince Hui and that the consort had committed debauchery, implicating over a thousand people.

sentences.zh: 鑒等奏其妄，廢安泛為庶人，幽鳳陽，安涘亦革爵。

translations.literal: He Jian and the others memorialized that the charges were false; Anfan was degraded to commoner status and imprisoned at Fengyang, and An Si was also stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: He Jian and his colleagues reported the accusations groundless; Anfan was reduced to commoner status and confined at Fengyang, and An Si was also deprived of his title.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十七年，睦□審薨。

translations.literal: In Jiajing year seventeen Zhu Mu□shen died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mu□shen died in Jiajing 17.

sentences.zh: 子勤熄先卒，孫莊王朝堈嗣，三十年薨。

translations.literal: His son Qinxie had died earlier; the grandson Prince Zhuang Zhu Chaogang succeeded and died in year thirty.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qinxie had predeceased him; the grandson Zhu Chaogang, Prince Zhuang, succeeded and died in year thirty.

sentences.zh: 子敬王在鋌嗣，萬歷十年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Jing Zhu Zaijin succeeded; in Wanli year ten he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Zaijin, Prince Jing, succeeded and died in Wanli 10.

sentences.zh: 子端王肅溱嗣，薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Duan Zhu Suqin succeeded and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Suqin, Prince Duan, succeeded and died.

sentences.zh: 子恭枵嗣。

translations.literal: His son Gong Zhu Zongxiao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Zongxiao, Prince Gong, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十四年冬，李自成攻開封，恭枵出庫金五十萬，餉守陴者，懸賞格，殪一賊予五十金。

translations.literal: In the winter of Chongzhen year fourteen Li Zicheng attacked Kaifeng; Zongxiao took out five hundred thousand taels from the treasury to pay the wall defenders, posted a reward scale, and offered fifty taels of gold for each bandit killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Chongzhen 14 Li Zicheng besieged Kaifeng; Zhu Zongxiao drew five hundred thousand taels from the treasury to pay the defenders on the walls, posted a bounty schedule, and promised fifty taels of gold for every rebel slain.

sentences.zh: 賊穴城，守者投以火，賊被爇死，不可勝計，乃解圍去。

translations.literal: The bandits tunneled under the city; the defenders cast fire down, and the bandits were burned to death beyond counting, whereupon the siege was raised and they departed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels mined the walls; the defenders dropped fire into the tunnels, burning countless rebels alive, and the besiegers finally lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，帝下詔褒獎，且加勞曰：「此高皇帝神靈憫宗室子孫維城莫固，啟王心而降之福也。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the emperor issued an edict of praise and added words of encouragement, saying: "This is the divine spirit of the founding emperor pitying his clan descendants because the wall of state was not firm, opening the prince's heart and bestowing blessing upon him."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the emperor issued a commendatory edict, adding: "The founding emperor's spirit has pitied his clan because the royal bulwark was weak, moved the prince's heart, and sent down this blessing."

sentences.zh: 其年四月，自成再圍汴，築長圍，城中樵采路絕。

translations.literal: That year in the fourth month Zicheng again surrounded Bian, built a long encirclement, and within the city the routes for gathering firewood were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, in the fourth month, Zicheng again besieged Bian, threw up a long blockade, and cut off every path by which the city could gather fuel.

sentences.zh: 九月，賊決河灌城，城圮，恭枵從後山登城樓，率宮妃及寧鄉、安鄉、永壽、仁和諸王露棲雨中數日。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the bandits breached the river to flood the city; the walls collapsed; Zongxiao ascended a tower from the rear hill, leading palace consorts and the princes of Ningxiang, Anxiang, Yongshou, Renhe, and others to sleep exposed in the rain for several days.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the rebels broke the river banks to inundate the city; as the walls gave way, Zhu Zongxiao climbed a tower on the rear hill and led palace ladies and the princes of Ningxiang, Anxiang, Yongshou, Renhe, and the rest to shelter unsheltered in the rain for days.

sentences.zh: 援軍駐河北，以舟來迎，始獲免。

translations.literal: Relief troops were stationed north of the river; they came by boat to welcome him, and only then did he escape.
translations.idiomatic: Relief forces camped on the north bank of the river and sent boats to fetch him; only then was he saved.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜書慰勞，並賜帑金文綺，命寄居彰德。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor granted a letter of consolation and reward, also bestowing treasury gold and patterned silks, and ordered him to lodge at Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, the emperor sent a letter of comfort and reward, together with treasury gold and brocade, and ordered him to reside temporarily at Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 汴城之陷也，死者數十萬，諸宗皆沒，府中分器寶藏書盡淪於巨浸。

translations.literal: When Bian city fell, several hundred thousand died; all members of the clan perished, and the ritual vessels, treasures, and books in the princely residence were entirely lost in the great inundation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fall of Kaifeng hundreds of thousands perished; the entire clan within the walls was wiped out, and the fief's ritual vessels, treasures, and books were all swallowed by the flood.

sentences.zh: 逾年，乃從水中得所奉高帝、高後金容，迎至彰德奉焉。

translations.literal: More than a year later, only then were the golden images of the founding emperor and Empress Gao that had been enshrined recovered from the water and welcomed to Zhangde to be served.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the gilded portraits of the founding emperor and Empress Gao were recovered from the waters and brought to Zhangde for veneration.

sentences.zh: 久之，王薨，贈謚未行，國亡。

translations.literal: After a long time the prince died; posthumous honors were not conferred, and the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: In time the prince died before posthumous titles could be granted, and the fief was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 其孫南走，死於廣州。

translations.literal: His grandson fled south and died at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson fled southward and died at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 鎮平王有爌，定王第八子。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhenping Zhu Youhuang was the eighth son of Prince Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youhuang, Prince of Zhenping, was the eighth son of Prince Ding.

sentences.zh: 嗜學，工詩，作《道統論》數萬言。

translations.literal: He was fond of learning and skilled at poetry; he composed Discourse on the Moral Way in tens of thousands of words.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and excelled at verse, composing the Discourse on the Moral Way in tens of thousands of words.

sentences.zh: 又采歷代公族賢者，自夏五子迄元太子真金百餘人，作《賢王傳》若干卷。

translations.literal: He also collected worthy men of the noble clans through the ages, from the Five Sons of Xia down to the Yuan crown prince Jingjin—more than a hundred persons—and composed Biographies of Worthy Princes in several volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He also gathered worthy princes and nobles from successive dynasties, from the Five Sons of Xia down to the Yuan crown prince Jingjin—more than a hundred in all—and compiled Biographies of Worthy Princes in several volumes.

sentences.zh: 博平王安水戍，惠王第十三子。
