translations.literal: Prince of Boping Zhu An Shuiyu was the thirteenth son of Prince Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu An Shuiyu, Prince of Boping, was Prince Hui's thirteenth son.

sentences.zh: 惠王有子二十五人，而安水戍獨賢，嘗輯《貽後錄》、《養正錄》諸書。

translations.literal: Prince Hui had twenty-five sons, but An Shuiyu alone was worthy; he once compiled Records for Posterity, Records of Nurturing Rectitude, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: Though Prince Hui had twenty-five sons, An Shuiyu alone was regarded as virtuous; he compiled such works as Records for Posterity and Records of Nurturing Rectitude.

sentences.zh: 勤於治生，田園僮奴車馬甚具。

translations.literal: He was diligent in managing his livelihood; his fields, gardens, servants, horses, and carriages were very complete.
translations.idiomatic: He worked hard at household economy and kept fields, gardens, servants, horses, and carriages in ample supply.

sentences.zh: 賓客造門，傾己納之。

translations.literal: When guests came to his door, he emptied himself to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When guests arrived he gave them his full hospitality.

sentences.zh: 其時稱名德者，必曰博平。

translations.literal: At that time anyone spoken of for noted virtue was sure to name Boping.
translations.idiomatic: In those days, whenever men praised moral renown, they pointed to Boping.

sentences.zh: 南陵王睦柍，悼王第九子，敏達有識。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanling Zhu Muzhao was the ninth son of Prince Dao, sharp-witted and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Muzhao, Prince of Nanling, ninth son of Prince Dao, was quick-minded and discerning.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十一年，御史林潤言：「天下財賦，歲供京師米四百萬石，而各籓祿歲至八百五十三萬石。

translations.literal: In Jiajing year forty-one Censor Lin Run said: "The empire's fiscal revenue supplies four million shi of grain yearly to the capital, while the various fiefs' stipends reach eight million five hundred thirty thousand shi yearly.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 41 Censor Lin Run memorialized: "The empire's tax grain sent yearly to the capital amounts to four million shi, while stipends to the various fiefs total eight million five hundred thirty thousand shi a year.

sentences.zh: 山西、河南存留米二百三十六萬三千石，而宗室祿米五百四萬石。

translations.literal: Shanxi and Henan retained grain totaled two million three hundred sixty-three thousand shi, while clan stipend grain was five million four hundred thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The retained grain of Shanxi and Henan came to two million three hundred sixty-three thousand shi, yet stipend grain for the imperial clan alone was five million four hundred thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 即無災傷蠲免，歲輸亦不足供祿米之半。

translations.literal: Even without disaster, injury, or remission, the yearly delivery would still not suffice to supply even half the stipend grain.
translations.idiomatic: Even if no calamity struck and no exemptions were granted, annual deliveries would still fall short of half the stipend grain required.

sentences.zh: 年復一年，愈加蕃衍，勢窮弊極，將何以支！」

translations.literal: Year after year the clan grows ever more numerous; when resources are exhausted and abuses extreme, how can it be sustained!"
translations.idiomatic: Year by year the clan multiplies; when means are spent and abuses reach their limit, what will support it!"

sentences.zh: 事下諸王議。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down for discussion among the princes.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the princes for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 明年，睦柍條上七議：請立宗學以崇德教，設科選以勵人才，嚴保勘以杜冒濫，革冗職以除素餐，戒奔競以息饕貪，制拜掃以廣孝思，立憂制以省祿費。

translations.literal: The next year Muzhao itemized seven proposals: request establishing a clan school to exalt moral teaching; establishing examination selection to encourage talent; strict verification of lineage to stop false claims; abolishing redundant offices to remove those eating salary without work; warning against frantic competition to quell gluttonous greed; regulating tomb visits to broaden filial remembrance; establishing mourning regulations to economize stipend expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Muzhao submitted seven detailed proposals: establish clan schools to elevate moral instruction; hold examinations to encourage talent; tighten genealogical checks to block impostors; cut redundant posts to rid the rolls of sinecures; restrain frantic ambition to curb gluttonous greed; regulate grave visits to deepen filial duty; and institute mourning rules to reduce stipend costs.

sentences.zh: 詔下廷臣參酌之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered court ministers to deliberate on them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the court ministers to weigh the proposals.

sentences.zh: 其後諸籓遂稍稍陳說利弊，尚書李春芳集而上焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter the various fiefs gradually stated benefits and harms, and Minister Li Chunfang collected and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the various fiefs one by one aired the pros and cons, and Minister Li Chunfang gathered their views and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 及頒《宗籓條例》，多采睦柍議云。

translations.literal: When Regulations for the Imperial Clan was promulgated, Muzhao's proposals were largely adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Regulations for the Imperial Clan was issued, most of its provisions drew on Muzhao's recommendations.

sentences.zh: 鎮國中尉睦□挈，字灌甫，鎮平王諸孫。

translations.literal: State Pacification Commandant Zhu Mu□qie, style Guanfu, was a grandson of the Prince of Zhenping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mu□qie, State Pacification Commandant, whose style was Guanfu, was a grandson of the Prince of Zhenping.

sentences.zh: 父奉國將軍安河以孝行聞於朝，璽書旌賚。

translations.literal: His father, State Supporting General Zhu Anhe, was noted at court for filial conduct; an imperial letter commended and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhu Anhe, State Supporting General, was famed at court for filial piety and received an imperial commendation with gifts.

sentences.zh: 既沒，周王及宗室數百人請建祠。

translations.literal: After his death, the Prince of Zhou and several hundred clansmen petitioned to build a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: After he died, the Prince of Zhou and several hundred kinsmen petitioned for a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 詔賜祠額曰「崇孝」。

translations.literal: An edict granted the shrine plaque reading "Revering Filial Piety."
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted the plaque Revering Filial Piety for the shrine.

sentences.zh: 睦□挈幼端穎，郡人李夢陽奇之。

translations.literal: Mu□qie in youth was upright and clever; the local scholar Li Mengyang marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Mu□qie was precocious and keen; the county scholar Li Mengyang took him for a wonder.

sentences.zh: 及長，被服儒素，覃精經學，從河、洛間宿儒游。

translations.literal: When he grew up he dressed in Confucian simplicity, plunged deeply into classical learning, and followed the senior Ru scholars of the Yellow and Luo regions.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood, he wore the plain dress of a scholar, mastered the classics, and studied with eminent Confucians along the Yellow and Luo rivers.

sentences.zh: 年二十通《五經》，尤邃於《易》、《春秋》。

translations.literal: At twenty he had mastered the Five Classics and was especially deep in the Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: By twenty he had mastered the Five Classics and was especially profound in the Book of Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 謂本朝經學一稟宋儒，古人經解殘闕放失，乃訪求海內通儒，繕寫藏棄，若李鼎詐《易解》、張洽《春秋傳》，皆敘而傳之。

translations.literal: He said that this dynasty's classical learning wholly followed the Song Ru, while the ancients' classic commentaries were damaged, lost, and scattered; he therefore sought throughout the realm for accomplished Ru, copied and preserved what had been abandoned, such as Li Dingzha's Explanation of the Changes and Zhang Qia's Transmission of the Spring and Autumn—all of which he prefaced and transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: He held that Ming classical studies merely followed the Song school, while older commentaries lay broken and scattered; he therefore searched the empire for master scholars, copied and preserved neglected works—among them Li Dingzha's Explanation of the Changes and Zhang Qia's Transmission of the Spring and Autumn—and wrote prefaces to circulate them.

sentences.zh: 呂柟嘗與論《易》，歎服而去。

translations.literal: Lu Nan once debated the Changes with him, sighed in admiration, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Nan once disputed the Book of Changes with him, marveled, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 益訪購古書圖籍，得江都葛氏、章丘李氏書萬卷，丹鉛歷然，論者以方漢之劉向。

translations.literal: He further sought and purchased ancient books and maps, obtaining ten thousand volumes from the Ge family of Jiangdu and the Li family of Zhangqiu; his vermilion ink marks were clear, and discussants compared him to Liu Xiang of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He went on buying up antiquarian books and charts, acquiring ten thousand volumes from the Ge of Jiangdu and the Li of Zhangqiu; his annotations were meticulous, and critics likened him to Han dynasty's Liu Xiang.

sentences.zh: 築室東坡，延招學者，通懷好士，而內行修潔。

translations.literal: He built a studio at Eastern Slope, extended invitations to scholars, was broad-minded and fond of gentlemen, while his private conduct was cultivated and pure.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hall on the Eastern Slope, gathered scholars about him, was open-handed and hospitable to men of talent, and kept his household conduct scrupulously upright.

sentences.zh: 事親晨昏不離側，喪三年居外捨。

translations.literal: In serving his parents he did not leave their side morning or evening; in mourning he dwelt three years in an outer lodging.
translations.idiomatic: He attended his parents from dawn to dusk without leaving them; in mourning he lived three years in an outer chamber.

sentences.zh: 有弟五人，親為教督，盡推遺產與之。

translations.literal: He had five younger brothers; he personally taught and supervised them and yielded all his inherited property to them.
translations.idiomatic: He had five younger brothers whom he personally instructed, and he gave them his entire inheritance.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年舉文行卓異，為周籓宗正，領宗學。

translations.literal: In Wanli year five he was nominated for outstanding literary conduct, became clan administrator of the Zhou fief, and headed the clan school.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 5 he was recommended for exceptional learning and conduct, made clan administrator of the Zhou fief, and placed in charge of the clan school.

sentences.zh: 約宗生以三、六、九日午前講《易》、《詩》、《書》，午後講《春秋》、《禮記》，雖盛寒暑不輟。

translations.literal: He appointed clan students to lecture on the Changes, Odes, and Documents before noon on the third, sixth, and ninth days, and on the Spring and Autumn Annals and Record of Rites in the afternoon, never ceasing even in extreme cold or heat.
translations.idiomatic: He scheduled lectures for kinsmen on the third, sixth, and ninth of each month: the Changes, Odes, and Documents before noon, the Spring and Autumn Annals and Record of Rites after—never suspended, even in bitter cold or fierce heat.

sentences.zh: 所撰有《五經稽疑》六卷，《授經圖傳》四卷，《韻譜》五卷，又作《明帝世表》、《周國世系表》、《建文遜國褒忠錄》、《河南通志》、《開封郡志》諸書。

translations.literal: His writings included Six Questions on the Five Classics in six juan, Transmission of the Classics Illustrated in four juan, Rhyme Tables in five juan; he also composed Tables of Ming Emperors, Genealogy of the Zhou State, Record of Loyalists in the Jianwen Abdication, Gazetteer of Henan, Gazetteer of Kaifeng Prefecture, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Six Questions on the Five Classics in six juan, Transmission of the Classics Illustrated in four juan, and Rhyme Tables in five juan, and also compiled Tables of Ming Emperors, Genealogy of the Zhou State, Record of Loyalists in the Jianwen Abdication, Gazetteer of Henan, Gazetteer of Kaifeng Prefecture, and other works.

sentences.zh: 巡撫御史褚鈇議稍減郡王以下歲祿，均給貧宗，帝遣給事中萬象春就周王議。

translations.literal: Provincial Censor Chu Tie proposed slightly reducing the annual stipends of princes below commandery rank and distributing them evenly to poor clansmen; the emperor sent Supervising Secretary Wan Xiangchun to consult with the Prince of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chu Tie of the provincial administration proposed trimming stipends for princes below commandery rank and redistributing the savings to impoverished clansmen; the emperor sent Supervising Secretary Wan Xiangchun to discuss the plan with the Prince of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 新會王睦□號於眾曰：「裁祿之謀起於睦□挈。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Xinhui Zhu Mu□hao cried out to the crowd: "The scheme to cut stipends arose from Mu□qie."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mu□hao, Prince of Xinhui, shouted before the assembly: "The plot to slash our stipends began with Mu□qie."

sentences.zh: 聚宗室千餘人擊之，裂其衣冠，上書抗詔。

translations.literal: More than a thousand clansmen gathered, beat him, tore his robes and cap, and memorialized in resistance to the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand kinsmen assembled, assaulted him, rent his robes and cap, and submitted a memorial defying the edict.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，廢睦□為庶人。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and degraded Mu□ to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and reduced Zhu Mu□ to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 睦 □挈屢疏引疾乞休，詔勉起之。

translations.literal: Zhu Mu □qie repeatedly memorialized citing illness and begging to retire; an edict urged him to rise and resume duty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mu □qie repeatedly memorialized on grounds of illness asking to resign, but edicts pressed him to return to office.

sentences.zh: 又三年卒，年七十。

translations.literal: Three years later he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 宗人頌功德者五百人，詔賜輔國將軍，禮葬之，異數也。

translations.literal: Five hundred clansmen praised his merit and virtue; an edict granted him the title Auxiliary State General and honored him with a ceremonial burial—an extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred kinsmen acclaimed his virtues; the throne conferred on him the title Auxiliary State General and an exceptional ceremonial burial.

sentences.zh: 學者稱為西亭先生。

translations.literal: Scholars called him Master of the Western Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars styled him Master Xiting.

sentences.zh: 時有將軍安水侃者，一歲喪母，事其父以孝聞。

translations.literal: At that time there was a general, An Shuikan, who at one year old lost his mother and was famed for filial service to his father.
translations.idiomatic: About that time there was a general named An Shuikan who had lost his mother at the age of one and became renowned for filial devotion to his father.

sentences.zh: 父病革，刲臂為湯飲父，父良已。

translations.literal: When his father was critically ill, he cut his arm to make broth for his father to drink, and his father recovered well.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell mortally ill, he sliced his own arm to brew medicine for him, and his father recovered.

sentences.zh: 年七十，追念母不逮養，服衰廬墓三年，詔旌其門。

translations.literal: At age seventy, recalling that he could not care for his mother in time, he wore mourning, built a hut by the grave for three years; an edict commended his gate.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy, lamenting that he had never been able to nurse his mother, he wore mourning and dwelt in a hut beside her tomb for three years; the court commended his household with an imperial testimonial.

sentences.zh: 素精名理，聲譽大著，人稱睦□挈為「大山」，安水侃為「小山」云。

translations.literal: He had long excelled in Neo-Confucian principles; his reputation was great. People called Zhu Mu□qie "Great Mountain" and An Shuikan "Little Mountain," it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Long versed in philosophical learning, he enjoyed wide renown; men dubbed Zhu Mu□qie the "Great Mountain" and An Shuikan the "Little Mountain."

sentences.zh: 又勤熨者，鎮國中尉也，嘉靖中，上書曰：「陛下躬上聖之資，不法古帝王兢業萬歲，擇政任人，乃溺意長生，屢修齋醮，興作頻仍。

translations.literal: There was also Qin Yun, a Pacification State lieutenant, who in the Jiajing era memorialized: "Your Majesty personally bears supreme-sage endowment, yet unlike ancient emperors' diligent toil for ten thousand years, you select policies and employ men—then you drown your mind in longevity, repeatedly perform fasting sacrifices, and construction rises without cease.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Qin Yun, a lieutenant of the Pacification State rank, who during Jiajing submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty possesses the gifts of a sage on high, yet unlike the ancient monarchs who toiled in diligence for the throne's ten thousand years, choosing policies and appointing worthy men, you have set your heart on immortality, held repeated fasting rites, and launched one construction project after another.

sentences.zh: 數年來朝儀久曠，委任非人，遂至賄賂公行，刑罰倒置，奔競成風，公私殫竭，脫有意外變，臣不知所終。」

translations.literal: For years court ritual has long lain vacant, appointments are not the right people—hence bribery runs openly, punishments are inverted, scrambling for office has become the custom, public and private are exhausted; if by chance there is an unforeseen change, your servant does not know how it will end.
translations.idiomatic: For years court ceremony has lain in neglect and unworthy men hold power, until bribery walks openly in the streets, punishments are meted out upside down, office-seeking has become the prevailing wind, and both state and household stand drained. Should any unforeseen calamity strike, your servant cannot see how this will end.

sentences.zh: 帝覽疏怒，坐誹謗，降庶人，幽鳳陽。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial in anger, convicted him of slander, reduced him to commoner, and imprisoned him in Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial in a fury, convicted him of slander, reduced him to commoner status, and confined him at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 子朝已賜名，以罪人子無敢為請封者，上書請釋父罪，且陳中興四事，詔並禁錮。

translations.literal: His son Chao had already been granted a name; as a convicted man's son none dared plead enfeoffment for him. He memorialized asking release of his father's crime and also set forth four matters for dynastic revival; an edict confined them both.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chao had already received a personal name, but as the son of a convicted man none dared seek a fief for him; Chao memorialized asking pardon for his father and laid out four proposals for restoring the dynasty—whereupon edicts placed both father and son under confinement.

sentences.zh: 穆宗登極，釋歸，命有司存恤。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, they were released and returned; he ordered the responsible offices to preserve and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, father and son were released and the responsible authorities were ordered to look after them.

sentences.zh: 楚昭王楨，太祖第六子。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao of Chu, Zhu Zhen, was the Founding Emperor's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhen, Prince Zhao of Chu, was the sixth son of the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 始生時，平武昌報適至，太祖喜曰：「子長，以楚封之。」

translations.literal: When he was first born, word that Wuchang had been pacified came just then; the Founding Emperor rejoiced and said: "When the son grows, enfeoff him in Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He was born just as news arrived that Wuchang had been pacified; the founding emperor rejoiced and said, "When my son comes of age, I shall enfeoff him in Chu.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年封楚王。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year three he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 十四年就籓武昌。

translations.literal: In year fourteen he took up his fief at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he went to his fief at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 嘗錄《御注洪範》及《大寶箴》置座右。

translations.literal: He once copied the Imperially Annotated Great Plan and Great Treasure Admonition and placed them at his seat's right.
translations.idiomatic: He copied the Imperially Annotated Great Plan and the Admonition of the Great Treasure and kept them at his desk.

sentences.zh: 十八年四月，銅鼓、思州諸蠻亂，命楨與信國公湯和、江夏侯周德興帥師往討。

translations.literal: In year eighteen, fourth month, the barbarians of Tonggu, Sizhou, and others rebelled; he ordered Zhen, together with Duke of Xin State Tang He and Marquis of Jiangxia Zhou Dexing, to lead troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year eighteen the peoples of Tonggu, Sizhou, and neighboring districts rose in revolt; the emperor ordered Zhu Zhen, together with Duke Tang He of Xin and Marquis Zhou Dexing of Jiangxia, to lead an expedition against them.

sentences.zh: 和等分屯諸洞，立柵與蠻人雜耕作。

translations.literal: He and the others divided encampments among the caves, set up palisades, and farmed mixed with the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He and the others garrisoned the mountain passes, threw up stockades, and farmed alongside the tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 久之，擒其渠魁，餘黨悉潰。

translations.literal: After a long while they captured the ringleaders; the remaining bands all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In time they seized the rebel chiefs and the rest of the host scattered.

sentences.zh: 三十年，古州蠻叛，帝命楨帥師，湘王柏為副，往征。

translations.literal: In year thirty the Guzhou barbarians rebelled; the emperor ordered Zhen to command the army, with Prince of Xiang Bo as deputy, to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty the peoples of Guzhou revolted; the emperor ordered Zhu Zhen to take command with the Prince of Xiang, Zhu Bo, as his second, and march against them.

sentences.zh: 楨請餉三十萬，又不親蒞軍。

translations.literal: Zhen requested thirty myriad in rations and again did not personally attend the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhen demanded three hundred thousand piculs in supplies and again failed to appear in person at the front.

sentences.zh: 帝詰責之，命城銅鼓衛而還。

translations.literal: The emperor interrogated and rebuked him, ordered him to fortify Tonggu Guard and return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sternly rebuked him, ordered the fortification of Tonggu Guard, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 是年，熒惑入太微，詔諭楨戒慎，楨書十事以自警。

translations.literal: That year Mars entered the Taiwei constellation; an edict instructed Zhen to be vigilant; Zhen wrote ten items to warn himself.
translations.idiomatic: That year Mars entered the Taiwei constellation; an edict urged Zhu Zhen to be on his guard, and he wrote down ten cautions for himself.

sentences.zh: 未幾，楨子巴陵王卒，帝復與敕曰：「舊歲熒惑入太微，太微天庭，居翼軫，楚分也。

translations.literal: Before long Zhen's son the Prince of Baling died; the emperor again issued an edict: "Last year Mars entered Taiwei; Taiwei is the celestial court, dwelling in Wings and Chariot—Chu's allotted region.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhu Zhen's son, the Prince of Baling, died; the emperor sent another edict: "Last year Mars entered Taiwei—that constellation is the celestial court, positioned in the Wings and Chariot station, which falls in the quarter allotted to Chu.

sentences.zh: 五星無故入，災必甚焉。

translations.literal: When the five planets enter without cause, disaster must be severe.
translations.idiomatic: When any of the five planets enter it without cause, calamity is sure to be grave.

sentences.zh: 爾子疾逝，恐災不止此，尚省慎以回天意。」

translations.literal: Your son departed swiftly in illness; I fear disaster does not stop here—still examine yourself and be cautious to turn back Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Your son has died young; I fear the omen may not end here—be ever watchful and restrained, that you may turn Heaven's mind.

sentences.zh: 至冬，王妃薨。

translations.literal: By winter the princess consort passed away.
translations.idiomatic: By winter the consort had died.

sentences.zh: 時初設宗人府，以楨為右宗人。

translations.literal: At that time the Clan Court was first established; Zhen was made Right Clan Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When the Clan Princes' Court was first established, Zhu Zhen was appointed its right administrator.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，進宗正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he was promoted to Chief Clan Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongle reign he was promoted to chief clan administrator.

sentences.zh: 二十二年薨。

translations.literal: In year twenty-two he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-second year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 子憲王季堄嗣。

translations.literal: His son the Prudent Prince Ji Ren succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Ji Ren, Prince Xian, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 事母鄧妃至孝。

translations.literal: He served his mother Consort Deng with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother, Lady Deng, with exceptional filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 英宗賜書獎諭。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong sent a letter commending and instructing him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong sent him a letter of praise and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 著《東平河間圖贊》，為士林所誦。

translations.literal: He wrote Illustrations and Encomia of Dongping and Hejian, which the scholarly community recited.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Illustrations and Encomia of Dongping and Hejian, widely read in scholarly circles.

sentences.zh: 八年薨。

translations.literal: In year eight he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 弟康王季埱嗣。

translations.literal: His younger brother the Vigorous Prince Ji Yang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhu Ji Yang, Prince Kang, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 天順六年薨。

translations.literal: In Tianshun year six he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of the Tianshun reign.

sentences.zh: 再從子靖王均□嗣，正德五年薨。

translations.literal: A great-grandnephew, the Tranquil Prince Jun□, succeeded; in Zhengde year five he died.
translations.idiomatic: A great-grandnephew, Zhu Jun□, Prince Jing, succeeded and died in Zhengde 5.

sentences.zh: 子端王榮水戒嗣，以仁孝著稱，武宗表曰「彰孝之坊」。

translations.literal: His son the Upright Prince Rong Shuijie succeeded, famed for benevolence and filial piety; Emperor Wuzong inscribed his plaque "Model of Manifest Filial Piety."
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Rong Shuijie, Prince Duan, succeeded and was renowned for benevolence and filial piety; Emperor Wuzong honored his gate with the plaque "Beacon of Filial Devotion."

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十三年薨。

translations.literal: In Jiajing year thirteen he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiajing 13.

sentences.zh: 子愍王顯榕嗣，居喪哀痛，遇慶禮卻賀。

translations.literal: His son the Lamented Prince Xian Rong succeeded; in mourning he was deeply grief-stricken, and when joyous rites came he declined congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Xian Rong, Prince Min, succeeded; in mourning he was consumed by grief, and when festivities arose he refused all congratulations.

sentences.zh: 端王婿儀賓沈寶與顯榕有隙，使人誣奏顯榕左右呼顯榕萬歲，且誘顯榕設水戲以習水軍。

translations.literal: The son-in-law Ceremonial Companion Shen Bao of Prince Duan had a rift with Xian Rong; he sent men to falsely memorialize that Xian Rong's attendants called "Long live Xian Rong," and moreover enticed Xian Rong to set up water games to drill a navy.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Bao, ceremonial companion married to the Prince of Duan's daughter, bore a grudge against Zhu Xian Rong; he had agents submit a false charge that Xian Rong's attendants hailed him as "ten thousand years," and lured the prince into staging aquatic games as naval drill.

sentences.zh: 世宗下其章，撫臣具言顯榕居喪能守禮。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong sent down the memorial; the provincial governor set forth in detail that Xian Rong in mourning could observe ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong referred the memorial to the provincial administration, which reported in detail that Zhu Xian Rong had scrupulously observed mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 寶坐誣，削為民。

translations.literal: Bao was convicted of false accusation and reduced to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Bao was found guilty of slander and stripped to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 子華奎幼，萬歷八年，始嗣爵。

translations.literal: His son Hua Kui was young; in Wanli year eight he finally inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hua Kui was still a child; he did not inherit until Wanli 8.

sentences.zh: 衛官王守仁上告曰：「遠祖定遠侯弼，楚王楨妃父也，遺瑰寶數十萬寄楚帑，為嗣王侵匿。」

translations.literal: A guard officer Wang Shouren reported: "A remote ancestor the Marquis of Dingyuan Bi was father to Prince of Chu's consort; he left several hundred thousand in precious gems deposited in Chu's treasury, usurped and hidden by succeeding princes.
translations.idiomatic: A guard officer named Wang Shouren petitioned: "Our distant forebear Bi, Marquis of Dingyuan—father to a consort of Prince Chu Zhu Zhen—left treasures worth hundreds of thousands deposited in the Chu treasury, which successive princes have embezzled.

sentences.zh: 詔遣中官清核。

translations.literal: An edict sent eunuchs to audit clearly.
translations.idiomatic: The throne dispatched palace eunuchs to conduct an audit.

sentences.zh: 華奎奏辨，且請避宮搜掘。

translations.literal: Hua Kui memorialized in defense and also begged to vacate the palace for search and excavation.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Kui memorialized in his own defense and even offered to vacate the palace so it could be searched and dug over.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received response.
translations.idiomatic: The court made no reply.

sentences.zh: 久之，系鞫王府承奉等，無所得。

translations.literal: After a long while they arrested and interrogated the prince's palace attendants and the like—nothing was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually the prince's palace staff were arrested and interrogated, but nothing was found.

sentences.zh: 時諸璫方以搜括希上意，不欲暴守仁罪。

translations.literal: At that time the eunuchs were just using seizures to court the emperor's wish and did not wish to expose Shouren's crime.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs were then gratifying the emperor with confiscatory searches and were loath to expose Wang Shouren's fabrications.

sentences.zh: 帝頗悟，罷其事。

translations.literal: The emperor came somewhat to understand and dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw through the affair and dropped it.

sentences.zh: 華奎乃奏上二萬金助三殿工。

translations.literal: Hua Kui then memorialized presenting twenty thousand in gold to aid the Three Halls works.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Kui then submitted twenty thousand taels of gold toward construction of the Three Halls.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，楚宗人華□等言：「華奎與弟宣化王華壁皆非恭王子。

translations.literal: In year thirty-one, Chu clansmen Zhu Hua□ and others said: "Hua Kui and his younger brother the Prince of Xuanhua Hua Bi are both not sons of the Respectful Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-one certain Chu kinsmen led by Zhu Hua□ declared: "Hua Kui and his younger brother Hua Bi, Prince of Xuanhua, are not sons of Prince Gong.

sentences.zh: 華奎乃恭王妃兄王如言子，抱養宮中。

translations.literal: Hua Kui was the son of the Respectful Prince's consort's elder brother Wang Ruyan, adopted and reared in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Kui is the son of Wang Ruyan, elder brother of Prince Gong's consort, and was secretly reared in the palace.

sentences.zh: 華壁則王如綍家人王玉子也。

translations.literal: Hua Bi was the son of Wang Yu, a household man of Wang Ruzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Bi is the son of Wang Yu, a servant in Wang Ruzhi's household.

sentences.zh: 華□妻，即如言女，知之悉。」

translations.literal: Hua□'s wife was precisely Ruyan's daughter and knew it all thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hua□'s wife is Wang Ruyan's daughter and knows the whole story.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎郭正域請行勘。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Guo Zhengyu requested that an investigation be conducted.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhengyu, vice minister of rites, urged a formal investigation.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈一貫右華奎，委撫按訊，皆言偽王事無左驗。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan sided with Hua Kui; he entrusted the provincial governor and censor to investigate—all said the false-prince affair had no corroborating evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan backed Hua Kui and referred the case to the provincial governor and touring censor, who all reported that there was no corroborating evidence of a pretender.

sentences.zh: 而華□妻持其說甚堅，不能決，廷議令覆勘。

translations.literal: But Hua□'s wife held to her claim very firmly; they could not decide; court deliberation ordered re-investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhu Hua□'s wife stuck stubbornly to her accusation, and with no resolution in sight the court ordered a fresh inquiry.

sentences.zh: 中旨以楚王襲封已二十餘年，宜治華□等誣罔。

translations.literal: A secret edict held that the Prince of Chu had held succession for more than twenty years; Zhu Hua□ and others' false accusations should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict ruled that the Prince of Chu had held the title for more than twenty years and that Zhu Hua□ and his fellows should be punished for malicious falsehood.

sentences.zh: 御史錢夢皋為一貫劾正域，正域發華奎行賄一貫事。

translations.literal: Censor Qian Menghu for Yiguan impeached Zhengyu; Zhengyu exposed Hua Kui's bribing of Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Qian Menghu, acting for Shen Yiguan, impeached Guo Zhengyu; Guo in turn exposed Hua Kui's bribes to Shen.

sentences.zh: 華奎遂訟言正域主使，正域罷去。

translations.literal: Hua Kui then sued saying Zhengyu was the mastermind; Zhengyu was dismissed and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Kui counter-sued, charging that Guo Zhengyu had orchestrated the accusation, and Guo was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 東安王英燧、武岡王華增、江夏王華□等皆言偽跡昭著，行賄有據。

translations.literal: Prince of Dong'an Ying Sui, Prince of Wugang Hua Zeng, Prince of Jiangxia Hua□, and others all said the fraud was manifest and bribery had evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Sui, Prince of Dong'an; Hua Zeng, Prince of Wugang; Zhu Hua□, Prince of Jiangxia; and others maintained that the imposture was obvious and the bribery well documented.

sentences.zh: 諸宗人赴都投揭。

translations.literal: The various clansmen went to the capital to lodge open accusations.
translations.idiomatic: Chu kinsmen traveled to the capital to file public petitions.

sentences.zh: 奉旨切責，罰祿、削爵有差。

translations.literal: Receiving an imperial order of stern rebuke, fines on stipends and reduction of titles were meted out by degree.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order they were sharply reprimanded and penalized with varying fines and reduction of ranks.

sentences.zh: 華□坐誣告，降庶人，錮鳳陽。

translations.literal: Hua□ was convicted of false accusation, reduced to commoner, imprisoned in Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hua□ was convicted of false accusation, reduced to commoner status, and confined at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，華奎輸賄入都，宗人遮奪之。

translations.literal: Before long Hua Kui transported bribes into the capital; clansmen intercepted and seized them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hua Kui sent bribes to the capital; clansmen waylaid the convoy and seized the goods.

sentences.zh: 巡撫趙可懷屬有司捕治。

translations.literal: Provincial Governor Zhao Kehuai ordered the responsible offices to arrest and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Governor Zhao Kehuai ordered the authorities to arrest and punish them.

sentences.zh: 宗人蘊□等方恨可懷治楚獄不平，遂大哄，毆可懷死。

translations.literal: Clansmen Zhu Yun□ and others were just resenting Kehuai's handling of the Chu case as unjust; they raised a great tumult and beat Kehuai to death.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen led by Zhu Yun□, still bitter that Zhao Kehuai had handled the Chu affair unfairly, raised a riot and beat the governor to death.

sentences.zh: 巡按吳楷以楚叛告。

translations.literal: Touring Censor Wu Kai reported Chu in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Wu Kai memorialized that Chu had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 一貫擬發兵會剿。

translations.literal: Yiguan drafted sending troops for joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yiguan drafted a plan to dispatch troops for a joint punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 命未下，諸宗人悉就縛。

translations.literal: Before the order was issued, all the clansmen were bound and taken.
translations.idiomatic: Before the order could be issued, all the kinsmen were taken into custody.

sentences.zh: 於是斬二人，勒四人自盡，錮高牆及禁閒宅者復四十五人。

translations.literal: Thereupon two were beheaded, four forced to take their own lives, and confined to the high wall and restricted dwellings were another forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Two were beheaded, four compelled to take their own lives, and forty-five more were immured in the high-walled compound or confined to vacant dwellings.

sentences.zh: 三十三年四月也。

translations.literal: It was the fourth month of year thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: This took place in the fourth month of year thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 自是無敢言楚事者。

translations.literal: From this no one dared speak of Chu affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From that day forward none dared speak of the Chu succession again.

sentences.zh: 久之，禁錮諸人以恩詔得釋，而華奎之真偽竟不白。

translations.literal: After a long while those under confinement were released under an amnesty edict, but whether Hua Kui was genuine or false was never clarified.
translations.idiomatic: In time those who had been confined were released under an amnesty, yet whether Hua Kui was legitimate was never settled.

sentences.zh: 其後，張獻忠掠湖廣，華奎募卒自衛，以張其在為帥。

translations.literal: Later, Zhang Xianzhong plundered Huguang; Hua Kui recruited troops to defend himself, appointing Zhang Qizai as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhang Xianzhong ravaged Huguang, Hua Kui raised a guard force and installed Zhang Qizai as its commander.

sentences.zh: 獻忠兵至武昌，其在為內應，執華奎沉之江，諸宗無得免者。

translations.literal: When Xianzhong's troops reached Wuchang, Qizai acted as inside agent, seized Hua Kui and drowned him in the river; none of the clansmen escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhong's army reached Wuchang, Zhang acted as a fifth column, seized Hua Kui, and drowned him in the Yangzi; not one of the Chu princes escaped.

sentences.zh: 武岡王顯槐，端王第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Wugang Xian Huai was the third son of Prince Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xian Huai, Prince of Wugang, was the third son of Prince Duan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十三年上書條籓政，請「設宗學，擇立宗正、宗表，督課親郡王以下子弟。

translations.literal: In Jiajing year forty-three he memorialized enumerating feudatory policy, requesting: "Establish a clan school, select and appoint clan chief and clan registrar, supervise instruction for sons and younger brothers from close prince of commandery rank down.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 43 he submitted a memorial outlining reforms to princely administration, proposing: "Establish a clan school, appoint a clan chief and registrar, and supervise the education of all princes and younger sons from commandery rank down.

sentences.zh: 十歲入學，月餼米一石，三載督學使者考績，陟其中程式者全祿之，五試不中課則黜之，給以本祿三之二。

translations.literal: Enter school at ten years, monthly grain stipend one shi per month; after three years the education-inspecting envoy examines merit—those who attain the standard receive full stipend; five trials failing the curriculum are dismissed, given two-thirds of original stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Enroll them at ten with a monthly ration of one shi of grain; after three years the education commissioner shall examine them—those who meet the standard receive full stipends; after five failures they shall be dismissed and granted two-thirds of their original allowance.

sentences.zh: 其庶人暨妻女，月餼六石，庶女勿加恩。」

translations.literal: Commoners and their wives and daughters receive six shi monthly; common daughters receive no added favor.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners and their wives and daughters shall receive six shi per month; no extra allowance shall be granted to daughters of degraded lines.

sentences.zh: 其後廷臣集議，多采其意。

translations.literal: Afterward court ministers assembled in deliberation and largely adopted his ideas.
translations.idiomatic: When the court later convened to debate the matter, his proposals were largely adopted.

sentences.zh: 齊王榑，太祖第七子。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Zhu Fu, the Founding Emperor's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fu, Prince of Qi, was the founding emperor's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the third year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He received his enfeoffment in Hongwu 3.

sentences.zh: 十五年就籓青州。

translations.literal: In year fifteen he took up his fief at Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen he went to his fief at Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十三年命王帥護衛及山東徐、邳諸軍從燕王北征。

translations.literal: In year twenty-three the prince was ordered to command his guard and the armies of Xuzhou and Pei in Shandong to follow the Prince of Yan on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three he was ordered to lead his guard and the Xuzhou and Pei forces of Shandong on the northern campaign under the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 二十四年復帥護衛騎士出開平。

translations.literal: In year twenty-four he again commanded his guard cavalry out through Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four he again led his guard cavalry out through Kaiping Pass.

sentences.zh: 時已令穎國公傅友德調發山東都司各衛軍出塞，諭王遇敵當自為隊，奏凱之時勿與諸將爭功。

translations.literal: At that time the Duke of Ying State Fu Youde had already been ordered to mobilize the guards of Shandong Provincial Command for service beyond the passes; the prince was instructed that when meeting the enemy he should form his own unit, and when reporting victory he should not vie with the generals for merit.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youde, Duke of Ying, had already been ordered to mobilize the Shandong garrisons for service beyond the frontier; the prince was instructed that in battle he should keep to his own detachment and, when reporting victory, not contend with the field commanders for credit.

sentences.zh: 榑數歷塞上，以武略自喜，然性凶暴，多行不法。

translations.literal: Fu several times traversed the frontier, pleased with himself for martial strategy, yet his nature was fierce and cruel and he often committed unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fu campaigned repeatedly on the northern frontier and prided himself on military prowess, yet he was violent by nature and habitually broke the law.

sentences.zh: 建文初，有告變者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen someone reported a plot.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwen reign someone denounced him for plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 召至京，廢為庶人，與周王同禁錮。

translations.literal: Summoned to the capital, degraded to commoner, and confined together with the Prince of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the capital, he was deposed to commoner status and confined together with the Prince of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 燕兵入金川門，急遣兵護二王。

translations.literal: When Yan troops entered Jinchuan Gate, he urgently dispatched troops to protect the two princes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army entered through Jinchuan Gate, the Yongle emperor urgently sent troops to protect the two deposed princes.

sentences.zh: 二王卒不知所以，大怖，伏地哭。

translations.literal: The two princes at last did not know the reason, were greatly terrified, and wept prostrate on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes knew nothing of what was happening, were terrified, and flung themselves to the ground weeping.

sentences.zh: 已知之，乃大喜。

translations.literal: Once they knew, they were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When they learned the truth, they rejoiced greatly.

sentences.zh: 成祖令王齊如故，榑益驕縱。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzu ordered the Prince of Qi's status restored as before; Fu grew all the more arrogant and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengzu restored Zhu Fu's princely status, whereupon he grew more arrogant and unrestrained than ever.

sentences.zh: 帝與書召來朝，面諭王無忘患難時。

translations.literal: The emperor sent him a letter summoning him to court audience and personally instructed the prince not to forget the time of hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to court by letter and admonished him face to face never to forget the days of adversity.

sentences.zh: □尃不悛，陰畜刺客，招異人術士為咒詛，輒用護衛兵守青州城，並城築苑牆斷往來，守吏不得登城夜巡。

translations.literal: Zhu □bo would not repent; he secretly kept assassins, recruited strange men and technicians for curses, constantly used guard troops to hold Qingzhou city, built garden walls joining the city to sever traffic—city guards could not mount the wall for night patrol.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu □bo refused to mend his ways; he secretly trained assassins, recruited sorcerers to cast curses, routinely deployed his guard to hold Qingzhou, and walled off the adjoining park to block all passage, so that municipal patrols could not even mount the walls by night.

sentences.zh: 李拱、曾名深等上急變，榑拘匿以滅口。

translations.literal: Li Gong, Zeng Ming Shen, and others reported an urgent plot; Fu detained and hid them to silence them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gong, Zeng Mingshen, and others submitted urgent reports of treason; Zhu Fu seized and silenced them to cover his tracks.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年詔索拱，諭榑改過。

translations.literal: In Yongle year three an edict demanded Gong be surrendered and instructed Fu to reform.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongle an edict demanded that Li Gong be handed over and admonished Zhu Fu to mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 是時，周王橚亦中浮言，上書謝罪，帝封其書示榑。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Zhou Su also fell under floating talk, submitted a letter begging pardon, and the emperor sealed his letter and showed it to Fu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Zhou, Zhu Su, had likewise been swayed by rumor and submitted a letter of repentance; the emperor had the letter sealed and shown to Zhu Fu.

sentences.zh: 明年五月來朝，廷臣劾榑罪。

translations.literal: The next year in the fifth month he came to court; court ministers impeached Fu for crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The following May he came to court, and the ministers impeached Zhu Fu on multiple counts.

sentences.zh: 榑厲聲曰：「奸臣喋喋，又欲效建文時耶！

translations.literal: Fu in harsh voice said: "Treacherous ministers chatter endlessly—do you wish again to act as in Jianwen times!
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fu shouted: "These treacherous ministers will not stop their clamor—do you mean to repeat the Jianwen years!

sentences.zh: 會盡斬此輩。」

translations.literal: When we meet I shall behead this lot entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When the time comes I shall behead the lot of you.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之不懌，留之京邸。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was displeased; he detained him at the capital residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense at what he heard and kept him at a capital residence.

sentences.zh: 削官屬護衛，誅指揮柴直等，盡出榑系囚及所造不法器械。

translations.literal: He stripped official staff and guards, executed Commander Chai Zhi and others, and fully produced Fu's imprisoned men and unlawfully made weapons.
translations.idiomatic: His staff and guard were stripped away; the guard commander Chai Zhi and others were executed, and all prisoners Zhu Fu had held and the illegal arms he had manufactured were brought forth.

sentences.zh: 群臣請罪教授葉垣等，帝曰：「王性凶悖，朕溫詔開諭至六七，猶不悟，教授輩如王何！

translations.literal: The ministers asked punishment for instructors Ye Yuan and others; the emperor said: "The prince's nature is fierce and perverse; I have sent warm edicts opening instruction six or seven times and he still does not understand—what can instructors do for such a prince!
translations.idiomatic: The ministers asked that his tutors Ye Yuan and others be punished; the emperor said: "The prince is violent and obstinate. I have sent him six or seven gentle admonitions, yet he will not mend his ways—what could his tutors have done with such a prince!

sentences.zh: 垣等先自歸發其事，可勿問。」

translations.literal: Yuan and others first returned on their own and exposed the affair; they may go unquestioned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and the others came forward of their own accord and exposed the plot; let them go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 榑既被留，益有怨言。

translations.literal: Fu, having been detained, grew all the more in resentful talk.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhu Fu was detained, his complaints grew all the more bitter.

sentences.zh: 是年八月，召其子至京師，並廢為庶人。

translations.literal: That year in the eighth month he summoned his sons to the capital and together degraded them to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year the emperor summoned his sons to the capital and degraded them all to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年，福建妄男子樓濂詭稱七府小齊王，謀不軌。

translations.literal: In Xuande year three a deluded man of Fujian, Lou Lian, falsely claimed to be the Little Prince of Qi of the Seven Prefectures and plotted sedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuande a crackpot in Fujian, Lou Lian, falsely claimed to be the junior Prince of Qi of the seven prefectures and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 事覺，械至京，誅其黨數百人。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed he was shackled to the capital and several hundred of his party were executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed he was sent to the capital in fetters, and several hundred of his followers were put to death.

sentences.zh: 榑及三子皆暴卒，幼子賢赫安置廬州。

translations.literal: Fu and his three sons all died suddenly; the youngest son Xian He was settled at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fu and his three sons all died suddenly; the youngest, Xian He, was resettled at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年徙齊庶人、谷庶人置南京，敕守臣慎防。

translations.literal: In Jingtai year five the Qi commoner and Gu commoner were moved to Nanjing; an edict ordered guarding officials to guard carefully.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jingtai the deposed princes of Qi and Gu were transferred to Nanjing, and local officials were ordered to keep strict watch.

sentences.zh: 後谷庶人絕，齊庶人請得谷庶人第。

translations.literal: Later the Gu commoner line ended; the Qi commoner requested to obtain the Gu commoner's residence.
translations.idiomatic: After the Gu line died out, the Qi commoner asked to take over the Gu commoner's dwelling.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十三年釋高牆庶人長毚，榑曾孫也。

translations.literal: In Jiajing year thirteen the high-walled commoner Chang Chan was released—he was Fu's great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing the commoner Chang Chan, immured in the high-walled compound, was released; he was Zhu Fu's great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中有承彩者，亦榑裔。

translations.literal: In Wanli there was one Chengcai, also a descendant of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign there was a Chengcai, likewise a descendant of Zhu Fu.

sentences.zh: 齊宗人多凶狡，獨承彩頗好學云。

translations.literal: Many of the Qi clan were fierce and cunning; only Chengcai was rather fond of learning, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the Qi line were brutal and cunning; Chengcai alone, it is said, took to scholarship.

sentences.zh: 潭王梓，太祖第八子。

translations.literal: Prince of Tan Zi was the Founding Emperor's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zi, Prince of Tan, was the eighth son of the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the third year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He received his enfeoffment in Hongwu 3.

sentences.zh: 十八年就籓長沙。

translations.literal: In year eighteen he took up his fief at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen he went to his fief at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 梓英敏好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Zi was keen and clever, fond of learning, and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Zi was quick-witted and studious and excelled at prose.

sentences.zh: 嘗召府中儒臣，設醴賦詩，親品其高下，賚以金幣。

translations.literal: He once summoned the Confucian officials of his princedom, set out wine for verse-making, personally ranked them high and low, and rewarded them with gold and coin.
translations.idiomatic: He once gathered the scholars of his household, set out wine for a poetry contest, judged their work himself, and rewarded them with gold and cash.

sentences.zh: 妃于氏，都督顯女也。

translations.literal: His consort was the Lady Yu, daughter of Regional Commander Xian.
translations.idiomatic: His consort was Lady Yu, daughter of Regional Commander Yu Xian.

sentences.zh: 顯子琥，初為寧夏指揮。

translations.literal: Xian's son Hu at first served as commander in Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's son Yu Hu had first served as a garrison commander in Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 二十三年坐胡惟庸黨，顯與琥俱坐誅。

translations.literal: In year twenty-three for involvement in Hu Weiyong's faction Xian and Hu were both executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three, implicated in Hu Weiyong's conspiracy, Xian and Hu were both put to death.

sentences.zh: 梓不自安。

translations.literal: Zi did not feel at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zi grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使慰諭，且召入見。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to comfort and instruct him and moreover summoned him for audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to reassure him and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 梓大懼，與妃俱焚死。

translations.literal: Zi was greatly afraid and together with his consort burned themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zi and his consort burned themselves alive.

sentences.zh: 無子，除其封。

translations.literal: He had no sons; his enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir, and his princely title was abolished.

sentences.zh: 趙王□巳，太祖第九子。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Zhu □ji was the Founding Emperor's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu □ji, Prince of Zhao, was the founding emperor's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年生。

translations.literal: Born in Hongwu year two.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the second year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 次年受封，明年殤。

translations.literal: The next year he received enfeoffment; the year after he died in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed the following year and died in infancy the year after.

sentences.zh: 子惠王泰堪嗣，九年薨。

translations.literal: Tan had a son, Prince of Hui Tai Kan, who succeeded; in year nine he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tan's son Tai Kan, Prince of Hui, succeeded him and died in the ninth year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 子莊王陽鑄嗣，嘉靖二年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince of Zhuang Yang Zhu succeeded; in Jiajing year two he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yang Zhu, Prince of Zhuang, succeeded and died in the second year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 莊王在位久，世子當漎，當漎子健杙皆前卒，健杙子端王觀□定嗣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhuang reigned long; heir apparent Dang Cheng, Dang Cheng's son Jian Yi, all died before him; Jian Yi's son Prince of Duan Guan □ding succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhuang reigned for many years; his heir Dang Cheng and Cheng's son Jian Yi both predeceased him, and Jian Yi's son Guan □ding, Prince of Duan, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 狎典膳秦信等，遊戲無度，挾娼樂，裸男女雜坐。

translations.literal: He was intimate with pantry officer Qin Xin and others, played without limit, kept singing girls, and sat naked with men and women mixed.
translations.idiomatic: He kept company with his pantry officer Qin Xin and others, indulged in endless revelry, kept prostitutes and musicians, and sat naked with men and women mingled together.

sentences.zh: 左右有忤者，錐斧立斃，或加以砲烙。

translations.literal: Those at his side who crossed him were killed on the spot with awl and axe, or subjected to branding torture.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who crossed him was killed on the spot with awl or axe, or put to the branding torture.

sentences.zh: 信等乘勢殘殺人。

translations.literal: Xin and others took advantage of their power to slaughter people.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xin and his clique used their influence to murder at will.

sentences.zh: 館陶王當淴亦淫暴，與觀□定交惡，相訐奏。

translations.literal: Prince of Guantao Dang Hu was also licentious and violent; he and Guan □ding were on bad terms and denounced each other in memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Hu, Prince of Guantao, was likewise debauched and brutal; he and Guan □ding became enemies and filed charges against each other.

sentences.zh: 帝念觀□定尚幼，革其祿三之二，逮誅信等，亦革當淴祿三之一。

translations.literal: The emperor considering Guan □ding was still young reduced his stipend by two-thirds; when Xin and others were arrested and executed, Dang Hu's stipend was also cut by one-third.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that Guan □ding was still young, the emperor cut his stipend by two-thirds; after Qin Xin and his gang were executed, Dang Hu's stipend was cut by one-third as well.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，觀□定薨。

translations.literal: In year twenty-eight Guan □ding died.
translations.idiomatic: Guan □ding died in year twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子恭王頤坦嗣，有孝行，捐邸中田湖，贍貧民，辭常祿，給貧宗。

translations.literal: His son Prince of Gong Yi Tan succeeded; he had filial conduct, donated fields and lakes in the residence to support the poor, declined his regular stipend, and gave to poor clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yitan, Prince of Gong, succeeded; noted for filial piety, he donated estate fields and ponds to feed the poor, declined part of his regular stipend, and gave to impoverished kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 前後七賜璽書嘉勞。

translations.literal: Seven times before and after he was granted sealed letters of praise and reward.
translations.idiomatic: The throne seven times sent him sealed letters of commendation.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十二年薨。

translations.literal: In Wanli year twenty-two he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-second year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 世子壽金爵先卒，弟敬王壽錚嗣，二十八年薨。

translations.literal: Heir apparent Shou Jin Jue died first; younger brother Prince of Jing Shou Zheng succeeded; in year twenty-eight he died.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Shou Jinjue predeceased him; his younger brother Shou Zheng, Prince of Jing, succeeded and died in year twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 弟憲王壽鋐嗣，崇禎九年薨。

translations.literal: Younger brother Prince of Xian Shou Peng succeeded; in Chongzhen year nine he died.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shou Peng, Prince of Xian, succeeded and died in the ninth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 弟肅王壽鏞嗣，薨。

translations.literal: Younger brother Prince of Su Shou Yong succeeded and died.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shou Yong, Prince of Su, succeeded and died.

sentences.zh: 子以派嗣，十五年，大清兵克兗州，被執死。

translations.literal: Son Yi Pai succeeded; in year fifteen Qing troops took Yanzhou and he was captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yipai succeeded; in year fifteen Qing forces captured Yanzhou and he was taken and killed.

sentences.zh: 弟以海轉徙台州，張國維等迎居於紹興，號魯監國。

translations.literal: Younger brother Yihai moved about to Taizhou; Zhang Guowei and others welcomed him to Shaoxing, styling him Supervisor of State of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yihai fled to Taizhou; Zhang Guowei and others installed him at Shaoxing as Supervisor of State for Lu.

sentences.zh: 順治三年六月，大兵克紹興，以海遁入海。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi year three sixth month great troops took Shaoxing; Yihai fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Shunzhi the Qing army took Shaoxing and Yihai fled to sea.

sentences.zh: 久之，居金門，鄭成功禮待頗恭。

translations.literal: After long time he dwelt at Jinmen; Zheng Chenggong treated him with considerable courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he lived on Kinmen, where Zheng Chenggong treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 既而懈，以海不能平，將往南澳。

translations.literal: Before long slackening; Yihai could not be appeased and was about to go south to Nan'ao.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chenggong slackened in his courtesy; unable to win Yihai over, and learning that Yihai meant to sail for Nan'ao,

sentences.zh: 成功使人沉之海中。

translations.literal: Chenggong had men sink him in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong had him drowned at sea.

sentences.zh: 歸善王當沍，莊王幼子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Guishan Dang Hong was the Prince of Zhuang's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Hong, Prince of Guishan, was the youngest son of the Prince of Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 正德中，賊攻兗州，帥家眾乘城，取護衛弓弩射卻賊。

translations.literal: In Zhengde years bandits attacked Yanzhou; he led household troops onto the wall, took guard crossbows and shot the bandits back.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign bandits attacked Yanzhou; he led his household onto the walls and drove them off with his guard's crossbows.

sentences.zh: 降敕獎諭，遂以健武聞。

translations.literal: An edict of praise and instruction was sent down; he then became known for martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent down a commendatory edict, and he won renown for martial valor.

sentences.zh: 時有卒袁質與舍人趙巖俱家東平，武斷為鄉人所惡。

translations.literal: At the time there was a soldier Yuan Zhi and a household attendant Zhao Yan, both with homes in Dongping, who bullied the neighborhood and were hated by the people.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a soldier, Yuan Zhi, and a household attendant, Zhao Yan, both domiciled in Dongping, ruled the countryside by force and were loathed by their neighbors.

sentences.zh: 吏部主事梁谷，亦東平人，少不檢，倚惡少為助，既貴，頗厭苦之，又與千戶高乾有怨。

translations.literal: Ministry of Personnel registrar Liang Gu, also a man of Dongping, in youth was unrestrained and relied on ruffians for help; once elevated he grew quite weary of them, and also had a grudge with chiliarch Gao Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Gu, a registrar in the Ministry of Personnel and likewise from Dongping, had been wild in his youth and leaned on local toughs; once he rose in rank he came to resent them, and he also bore a grudge against chiliarch Gao Qian.

sentences.zh: 正德九年，谷邑人西鳳竹、屈昂誑谷云：「質、巖且為亂。」

translations.literal: In Zhengde year nine fellow townsmen Xi Fengzhu and Qu Ang deceived Gu saying: "Zhi and Yan are about to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhengde his townsmen Xi Fengzhu and Qu Ang tricked him, saying, "Zhi and Yan are on the verge of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 谷心動，因並指乾等，告變於尚書楊一清。

translations.literal: Gu's heart was moved; he therefore also implicated Qian and others and reported a plot to Minister Yang Yiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Gu took the bait and, implicating Qian and others as well, reported a conspiracy to Minister Yang Yiqing.

sentences.zh: 兵部議以大兵駐濟南伺變。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War deliberated stationing a large force at Jinan to watch for trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War proposed stationing a large force at Jinan to await developments.

sentences.zh: 先是，當沍數與質、巖校射。

translations.literal: Earlier Dang Hong had several times competed in archery with Zhi and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dang Hong had often competed in archery with Zhi and Yan.

sentences.zh: 至是當沍父莊王聽長史馬魁譖言當沍結質、巖欲反，虞禍及，奏於朝。

translations.literal: At this time Dang Hong's father the Prince of Zhuang listened to Chief Secretary Ma Kui's slander that Dang Hong had joined Zhi and Yan intending rebellion, fearing disaster would reach him, and memorialized the court.
translations.idiomatic: Now Dang Hong's father, the Prince of Zhuang, believing Chief Secretary Ma Kui's slander that his son was plotting with Zhi and Yan, fearing he would be implicated, memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝遣司禮太監溫祥、大理少卿王純、錦衣衛指揮韓端往按問。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Director of Ceremonies Wen Xiang, Vice Minister of Justice Wang Chun, and Guard Commander Han Duan to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the director of ceremonial Wen Xiang, vice minister of justice Wang Chun, and guard commander Han Duan to investigate.

sentences.zh: 祥等至，圍當沍第，執之。

translations.literal: When Xiang and the others arrived they surrounded Dang Hong's residence and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived they surrounded Dang Hong's mansion and arrested him.

sentences.zh: 祥等讞谷所指皆平人。

translations.literal: Xiang and the others judged that all Gu's accusations pointed to innocent people.
translations.idiomatic: They found that everyone Gu had named was innocent.

sentences.zh: 魁懼事敗，乃諷所厚陳環及術士李秀佐證之，復以書及賄抵鎮守太監畢真，使逮二人詰問。

translations.literal: Kui feared the affair would fail; he therefore prompted his favorite Chen Huan and technician Li Xiu to bear false witness, and again sent a letter and bribe to the garrison eunuch Bi Zhen to have the two men seized and interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, fearing exposure, induced his protégé Chen Huan and a sorcerer, Li Xiu, to give false testimony, and sent Bi Zhen, the garrison eunuch, a letter and bribe to have the two men seized and questioned.

sentences.zh: 已而二人以實對，書賄事亦為真所發。

translations.literal: Before long the two answered according to fact; the letter and bribe affair was also exposed by Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the two told the truth, and Bi Zhen also exposed the bribery.

sentences.zh: 於是御史李翰臣劾谷報怨邀功，長史魁惑王罔奏，宜即訊。

translations.literal: Thereupon Censor Li Hanchen impeached Gu for repaying grudges and inviting merit, and Chief Secretary Kui for deluding the prince and false memorial— they should be immediately interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Hanchen then impeached Gu for settling scores and seeking credit, and Kui for misleading the prince and filing a false report; both should be interrogated at once.

sentences.zh: 詔下翰臣獄，謫廣德州判官，免谷罪不問。

translations.literal: An edict put Hanchen in prison, demoted him to magistrate of Guangde prefecture, and exempted Gu from punishment without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Hanchen thrown into prison and demoted to magistrate of Guangde, while Gu went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 御史程啟充等疏言：「谷、魁鼓煽流言，死不蔽罪，縱首禍而謫言者，非國體。」

translations.literal: Censor Cheng Qichong and others memorialized: "Gu and Kui stirred up rumors; death cannot cover their crimes—yet the chief culprits go free while those who spoke truth are demoted: this is not the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Censors led by Cheng Qichong wrote: "Gu and Kui fanned seditious talk—crimes that merit death—yet the ringleaders go free while the truth-teller is punished: this shames the realm.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not respond.

sentences.zh: 廷臣議當沍罪，卒無所坐。

translations.literal: Court ministers deliberated Dang Hong's crime; in the end nothing could be proved against him.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated Dang Hong's guilt but could prove no treason.

sentences.zh: 以藏護衛兵器違祖制，廢為庶人。

translations.literal: For keeping guard weapons in violation of ancestral institutions he was degraded to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He was deposed to commoner status for hoarding guard arms in breach of ancestral law.

sentences.zh: 戍質等於肅州。

translations.literal: Zhi and others were banished to garrison duty at Suzhou in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and the others were banished to the Gansu prefecture of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 所連逮多瘐死，魁坐誣奏斬。

translations.literal: Many of those implicated died in prison of illness; Kui was executed for false memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Many of those caught up in the case died in custody; Kui was beheaded for his false report.

sentences.zh: 鳳竹、昂流口外。

translations.literal: Fengzhu and Ang were exiled beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Fengzhu and Ang were banished beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 中官送當沍之高牆，當沍大慟曰：「冤乎！」

translations.literal: The palace eunuch escorted Dang Hong to the high wall; Dang Hong wailed greatly, saying, "Wronged!"
translations.idiomatic: As eunuchs escorted Dang Hong to the high-walled compound he cried out in anguish, "I have been wronged!

sentences.zh: 觸牆死。

translations.literal: He struck the wall and died.
translations.idiomatic: He dashed his head against the wall and died.

sentences.zh: 聞者傷之。

translations.literal: Those who heard were grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard of it mourned him.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍當濆，鉅野王泰墱諸孫也，慷慨有志節。

translations.literal: Supporter-General of the State Dang Fen, a grandson of Prince of Juye Tai Yong and others, was generous and had resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Fen, Supporter-General of the State and a grandson of Tai Yong, Prince of Juye, was high-spirited and principled.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年上書請停郡縣主、郡縣君恤典，以蘇民困。

translations.literal: In Jiajing year three he submitted a memorial asking to stop condolence rites for commandery and county princesses to relieve the people's distress.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing he memorialized asking that funeral rites for commandery and county princesses be suspended to ease the people's burdens.

sentences.zh: 七年奏辭輔國將軍並子奉國將軍祿，佐疏運河。

translations.literal: In year seven he memorialized declining the stipends of Supporter-General and his son's Sustainer-General, to assist in dredging the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he asked to give up his own stipend as Supporter-General and his son's as Sustainer-General to help dredge the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 賜敕褒諭。

translations.literal: He was granted an edict of praise and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rewarded him with a commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 又上書言：「各籓郡縣主、郡縣君先儀賓沒者，故事儀賓得支半祿。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial saying: "In each fief, when commandery and county princesses' former ceremonial consorts have died, by precedent the consort drew half stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "When a commandery or county princess's ceremonial consort dies, precedent allows the consort half stipend.

sentences.zh: 今四方災傷，邊陲多事，民窮財盡，而各儀賓暴橫侈肆，多不法，請勿論品級，減其月給。」

translations.literal: Now calamity and injury on four sides, the frontier with many affairs, the people poor and wealth exhausted—yet each ceremonial consort is violent, extravagant, and lawless; I ask regardless of rank to reduce their monthly payment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet disasters afflict every quarter, the borders are troubled, and the people are destitute—while these consorts grow violent, extravagant, and lawless. I beg that their monthly allotments be cut without regard to rank.

sentences.zh: 明年又請以父子應得祿米佐振。

translations.literal: The next year he again asked to use the rice stipend father and son should receive to assist relief.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he offered his and his son's grain stipends for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 因勸帝法祖宗，重國本，裁不急之費，息土木之工。

translations.literal: He thereby admonished the emperor to follow the ancestors, esteem the foundation of the state, cut unurgent expenses, and cease earth-and-wood works.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the emperor to follow the founders, strengthen the dynastic foundation, slash needless spending, and halt construction projects.

sentences.zh: 詞甚愷切。

translations.literal: His words were very earnest and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: His language was earnest and moving.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其意，特敕褒之，不聽辭祿。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his intent, specially granted an edict praising him, and did not accept his declining stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his intent, sent a special commendation, and refused his offer to give up his stipend.

sentences.zh: 時東甌王健楸無子，上書言：「宗室所以蕃，由詐以媵子為嫡，糜費縣官。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Dongou Jian Qiu had no sons and submitted a memorial saying: "The imperial clan multiplies because of fraud making concubine sons into heirs, wasting the state treasury.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jian Qiu, Prince of Dongou, had no legitimate heir and wrote: "The clan swells because men fraudulently install concubines' sons as heirs, draining the treasury.

sentences.zh: 今臣無嫡嗣，請以所受府第屯廠盡歸魯府，待給新封，省民財萬一，乞著為例。」

translations.literal: Now I have no legitimate heir; I ask that the mansion, estates, and farms I have received all be returned to the Lu princedom, to await new enfeoffment, saving the people's wealth in the slightest degree—beg that this be made precedent.
translations.idiomatic: I have no legitimate son; let my residence, estates, and farms revert to the Lu princedom until a new heir is named—sparing the people, if only a little—and let this become precedent.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 奉國將軍健根，鉅野王陽鎣諸孫。

translations.literal: Sustainer-General of the State Jian Gen, a grandson of Prince of Juye Yang Jin and others.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Gen, Sustainer-General of the State, was a grandson of Yang Jin, Prince of Juye.

sentences.zh: 博通經術，年七十，猶縱談名理，亹亹不倦。

translations.literal: Thoroughly versed in the classics, at age seventy he still discoursed freely on principle, tirelessly.
translations.idiomatic: A master of the classics, at seventy he still held forth on philosophy without tiring.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，詔褒其賢孝。

translations.literal: In Jiajing years an edict praised his worth and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiajing an edict praised his learning and filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 子鎮國中尉觀熰，字中立，居母喪，蔬食逾年，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: Son Defender-Commandant of the State Guan Xi, style Zhongli, in mourning for his mother ate vegetables more than a year, grief wasting him to bones.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guan Xi, Defender-Commandant of the State, styled Zhongli, mourned his mother on vegetables for more than a year until grief had worn him to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 嘗繪《太平圖》上獻。

translations.literal: He once painted "Picture of Great Peace" and presented it upward.
translations.idiomatic: He once painted the "Picture of Great Peace" and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘉獎之，賜承訓書院名額並《五經》諸書。

translations.literal: The Jiajing Emperor commended him and granted the name quota for the Chengxun Academy together with the Five Classics and other books.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiajing Emperor praised him and granted the Chengxun Academy an official name-quota, along with the Five Classics and other canonical works.

sentences.zh: 弟觀以詩畫著名。

translations.literal: His younger brother Guan was famed for poetry and painting.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Guan won renown as a poet and painter.

sentences.zh: 同時鉅野中尉頤壟、安丘將軍頤墉，聲詩清拔。

translations.literal: At the same time Commandant of Juye Zhu Yilong and General Zhu Yiyong of Anqiu were known for verse clear and elevated in tone.
translations.idiomatic: Around the same time, Zhu Yilong, Commandant of Juye, and Zhu Yiyong, General of Anqiu, were admired for poetry of lucid, distinguished voice.

sentences.zh: 樂陵王頤□戔亦喜稱詩。

translations.literal: Prince of Leling Zhu Yi□jian also delighted in composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi□jian, Prince of Leling, likewise took pleasure in writing verse.

sentences.zh: 安丘王當隧，靖王曾孫，少孤，事祖父母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Prince of Anqiu Zhu Dangsui, a great-grandson of Prince Jing, was orphaned young and was known for serving his grandparents with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Dangsui, Prince of Anqiu, a great-grandson of Prince Jing, lost his parents early and was famed for his filial care of his grandparents.

sentences.zh: 曾孫頤堀好學秉禮，尤諳練典故。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Zhu Yiku loved learning and upheld ritual, and was especially well versed in historical precedents.
translations.idiomatic: His descendant Zhu Yiku was devoted to study and observance of ritual and was especially expert in institutional precedent.

sentences.zh: 籓邸中有大疑，輒就決。

translations.literal: When great doubts arose in the princely household, they would go to him for a decision.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a serious question arose in the princedom, the clan turned to him for judgment.

sentences.zh: 一意韜晦，監司守令希見其面。

translations.literal: He deliberately kept himself in obscurity, and provincial overseers and magistrates rarely saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: He deliberately lived in seclusion, and provincial officials seldom caught sight of him.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，猶手不廢書。

translations.literal: Past seventy years of age, he still never laid books aside by his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Even past seventy he never stopped reading and writing with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 魯府宗室壽金林，家兗州。

translations.literal: Shou Jinlin of the Lu princely line made his home in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Jinlin, a kinsman of the Lu princely house, was a native of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中為雲南通判，有聲績。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign he served as assistant prefect of Yunnan and won a reputation for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he served as assistant prefect of Yunnan and earned a solid record of accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 永明王由榔在廣西，以為右僉都御史，使募兵。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yongming, Zhu Youlang, was in Guangxi, he appointed him Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and ordered him to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Youlang, the Prince of Yongming, held Guangxi, he named him Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and charged him with recruiting soldiers.

sentences.zh: 值沙定州亂，兵不能集。

translations.literal: Just then Sha Dingzhou rose in revolt, and troops could not be assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion broke out at Sha Dingzhou, and he could not gather his forces.

sentences.zh: 孫可望兵至，壽金林知不免，張麾蓋往見之，行三揖禮曰：「謝將軍不殺不掠之恩。」

translations.literal: When Sun Kewang's army arrived, Shou Jinlin knew he could not escape; he spread his canopy of command and went to see him, performed three bows with joined hands, and said: "I thank the general for the grace of neither killing nor plundering."
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Kewang's troops arrived, Shou Jinlin knew his end was near; he went forward under his command canopy, bowed three times with hands joined, and said, "I thank you, General, for sparing the people killing and looting.

sentences.zh: 可望脅之降，不從。

translations.literal: Kewang pressed him to surrender, but he would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kewang then tried to force him to submit, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 系他所，使人誘以官，終不從。

translations.literal: He was bound and held elsewhere; men were sent to tempt him with office, yet in the end he would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: They imprisoned him elsewhere and sent envoys promising him office, but he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 從容題詩於壁，或以詩報可望，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Composedly he inscribed poems on the wall, or answered Kewang in verse, and was then put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Calmly he wrote poems on the wall and sometimes replied to Sun Kewang in verse; in the end he was killed.
